chapters.title: Chapter 1701: Combat Hall!
paragraphs: After realizing just how poor he truly was within Starfall Haven, Max finally understood that his one hundred and ten thousand Killing Points were practically nothing in the grand scheme of the Cosmic Ascension Conference.

Earlier, he had felt somewhat satisfied after seeing his Killing Points surpass one hundred thousand. After all, he had slaughtered countless participants, farmed multiple lives from demons, destroyed an entire battlefield region, and even discovered a hidden cave filled with those terrifying rainbow rabbits.

Yet after entering Starfall Haven and looking at the prices of the Divine Abilities, that confidence had completely vanished. The cheapest Tier I Divine Ability alone required ten million Killing Points.
Compared to that astronomical figure, his one hundred and ten thousand points seemed almost laughable. For the first time since entering the Eternal Hourglass, Max genuinely felt poor.

After leaving the Divine Ability Pavilion, Max began wandering throughout Starfall Haven while carefully observing the city around him. The city was far more prosperous than he had initially imagined.

Vast marketplaces stretched endlessly throughout the streets while enormous buildings rose high into the sky. Some areas were dedicated entirely to entertainment, containing restaurants, taverns, gathering halls, and various attractions where participants could temporarily relax from the constant slaughter taking place outside the city walls.

Other districts contained endless rows of shops selling treasures, cultivation resources, weapons, armor, pills, maps, inheritances, and information. Everywhere he looked, people were buying, selling, negotiating, and exchanging resources.
The city almost felt like a real civilization existing independently within the Eternal Hourglass rather than a temporary gathering point for participants in a cosmic battle royale.
However, Max was not interested in spending Killing Points.
He was interested in earning them.

As he walked through one district after another, he continuously searched for possible opportunities to increase his wealth. Unfortunately, despite the countless shops and facilities available, none of them provided the answer he was looking for.

Eventually, after spending quite some time searching, Max stopped a random human participant walking nearby and directly asked. "Do you know the fastest way to earn Killing Points inside Starfall Haven?"
The man immediately laughed after hearing the question, as though Max had asked something extremely obvious.

"If you want to earn Killing Points, then there is only one place you should visit," the man said while pointing toward a distant part of the city. "The Combat Hall. Most people who stay in Starfall Haven for any significant amount of time eventually end up there. Some become rich overnight while others lose everything they possess. If you have confidence in your abilities, then there is no better place in the entire city."
The moment Max heard those words, his interest was instantly captured.

After obtaining directions from the man, he immediately headed toward the Combat Hall. The farther he traveled through the city, the more crowded the streets became. Participants filled every visible road while excitement permeated the atmosphere.

Before long, a gigantic structure gradually appeared in the distance. The building towered high above the surrounding city like an ancient colosseum, its massive walls stretching endlessly while countless golden runes shimmered across its surface.
Above the entrance floated two enormous words formed entirely from golden light.
Combat Hall.
Yet despite the sheer size of the structure itself, what truly shocked Max was not the building.
It was the crowd.
The moment he arrived before the Combat Hall, even Max could not help but stop briefly.
People.
Everywhere he looked there were people.

The area surrounding the Combat Hall was so crowded that it resembled a sea of living beings. Hundreds of thousands of participants had gathered around the building, creating a scene unlike anything Max had witnessed since entering the Eternal Hourglass.

Humans occupied large portions of the crowd, but they were far from the only race present. Demons with dark skin and horns continuously moved through the masses while elegant elves could occasionally be seen among them as well.

The atmosphere buzzed with endless conversations, arguments, cheers, and excitement. Some participants appeared thrilled while others looked devastated. Many walked out smiling broadly while clutching newly acquired treasures. Others stumbled out looking as though they had just lost everything they owned.
The entire place felt alive.
The noise alone was overwhelming.

Cheers erupted constantly from within the Combat Hall. Heated discussions filled the surrounding streets. Participants continuously rushed inside while others hurried out to spread news regarding recent matches and results.
Looking at the enormous crowd gathered around the building, Max immediately understood why the man had directed him here.

If there truly existed a place within Starfall Haven where Killing Points changed hands in massive quantities, then it was undoubtedly this Combat Hall. Just from the sheer number of people gathered here, Max could tell that enormous fortunes were being won and lost every single moment.
A faint smile slowly appeared across his face.
It seemed that his journey toward earning the remaining three hundred and ninety thousand Killing Points required for the Genesis Trial might begin here.

After spending some time asking around and gathering information from the participants present inside the Combat Hall, Max gradually came to understand why this place had become the most crowded location in all of Starfall Haven.
The deeper he looked into the rules governing the Combat Hall, the more he realized that the place had been specifically designed to tempt participants into risking everything they possessed.
It was no wonder that such an overwhelming number of people had gathered here despite the dangers involved.

The rules themselves were surprisingly simple. Any participant could register and begin a challenge sequence. Once the challenge started, they would face one opponent after another in consecutive battles.

Every victory would reward them with Killing Points obtained from defeating their opponent, allowing their earnings to steadily increase as they continued winning. However, the true attraction of the Combat Hall was not these ordinary rewards.
The true attraction was the massive bonus granted to anyone capable of achieving ten consecutive victories.

If a participant successfully defeated ten opponents in a row without suffering a single defeat, they would immediately receive a reward of one million Killing Points on top of all the Killing Points they had already accumulated from those ten battles.
One million Killing Points.
Even Max could not help but feel his heart shake slightly after hearing that number.

chapters.title: Chapter 1702: Rules of the Combat Hall!
paragraphs: Earlier, he had gone through considerable effort to gather just over one hundred thousand Killing Points. He had slaughtered countless participants, repeatedly farmed lives from demons, and wiped out an entire battlefield region.

Yet all of that combined was only a fraction of what the Combat Hall offered for ten consecutive victories. Suddenly, the prices inside the Divine Ability Pavilion no longer seemed completely impossible.
If someone possessed enough strength and enough luck, they could theoretically earn tremendous amounts of Killing Points within a relatively short period of time.
However, as Max continued listening, he soon discovered why the rewards were so generous.
There was a catch.
A very dangerous catch.
The Combat Hall was not a place where participants could safely accumulate rewards over time. Instead, it was a place where fortunes could change hands in an instant.
Every Killing Point earned during a challenge sequence remained at risk until the participant either completed all ten victories or voluntarily withdrew.
If someone lost before reaching ten victories, then all the Killing Points they had accumulated throughout their challenge would immediately transfer to the person who defeated them.
In other words, a participant could spend hours fighting their way through multiple opponents, accumulate a large amount of Killing Points, and then lose everything in a single battle.
The winner would take it all.

Because of this rule, every match became increasingly valuable as a participant’s winning streak grew longer. Someone who had already won seven or eight consecutive battles would often become a walking treasure chest worth hundreds of thousands of Killing Points.
The stronger they became and the closer they moved toward the one-million-point reward, the more attractive they became as targets for other participants hoping to claim everything they had earned.

As Max listened to the explanations and watched the excited crowds surrounding the various arenas, he finally understood why the Combat Hall had become so popular. The system was incredibly risky, yet at the same time it was impossible to ignore.

The possibility of earning one million Killing Points from a single challenge was enough to attract countless geniuses. Every participant believed they could be the next person to achieve ten consecutive victories. Every participant believed they possessed the strength to succeed where others had failed.
Naturally, that confidence continuously drove people into the arenas despite knowing the risks involved.

The Combat Hall had essentially transformed combat itself into a form of gambling. Participants wagered their strength, their confidence, and their accumulated Killing Points every time they entered an arena.

Some emerged richer than ever before. Others lost everything they had spent hours or even days earning. Yet despite those dangers, the crowds only continued growing larger. The promise of rapid wealth and glory was simply too tempting for most participants to resist.

Standing amidst the sea of people, Max slowly looked toward the enormous battle arenas located at the center of the Combat Hall. As countless participants cheered, fought, and challenged one another around him, a faint smile gradually appeared on his face.
Compared to wandering the Eternal Hourglass searching for opportunities one by one, this place seemed far more efficient.

If the rewards truly matched what he had heard, then perhaps the Combat Hall would become the fastest path toward accumulating the five hundred thousand Killing Points he needed for the Genesis Trial.
With very high expectations, Max made his way through the bustling crowds toward the registration area of the Combat Hall. The place was even busier than the rest of the building.

Thousands of participants continuously moved back and forth while enormous crystal screens displayed rankings, active challengers, ongoing battles, and the amounts of Killing Points currently at stake.

Excited cheers erupted from nearby arenas every few moments while countless spectators discussed the strengths and weaknesses of different fighters. The entire atmosphere felt charged with anticipation and greed. Here, fortunes could be won in a matter of minutes, and everyone wanted a piece of it.
Eventually, Max arrived before a long registration counter. However, what caught his attention was not the counter itself but the creature sitting behind it.
It was a strange animal unlike anything Max had ever seen before.

The creature resembled a fox and a rabbit combined together. It possessed silver fur, long ears, bright golden eyes, and a fluffy tail that lazily swayed behind it. It sat atop a floating chair while casually reading through countless glowing screens hovering before it.
Despite its small appearance, Max could sense a strange pressure coming from the creature, making it clear that it was far from ordinary.
The moment Max approached the counter, the strange animal did not even look up.
Instead, it lazily spoke.
"Name."
Max raised an eyebrow slightly before replying.
"Max Morgan."
The creature’s ears twitched.
Immediately, several glowing runes appeared before it as though searching through some enormous database.
A few moments later, the strange animal finally looked up.
Its golden eyes briefly examined Max from head to toe.
Then it nodded.
"Registration successful."
Several glowing symbols appeared before Max before quickly disappearing.
The creature continued speaking in a calm and practiced tone.
"You are now officially registered within the Combat Hall. As a registered participant, you have two options available to you."
Max listened attentively.
The strange animal flicked its tail before continuing.

"The first option is to challenge an active participant currently undergoing the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial. If you defeat them, you immediately inherit all the Killing Points they have accumulated during their current challenge sequence."
At those words, Max’s eyes immediately brightened.
That sounded very profitable.
The creature continued.

"The second option is to begin your own Ten Consecutive Victory Trial. In that case, you will be placed into the queue and wait for your turn. Once selected, you will begin fighting consecutive opponents. Every victory increases your accumulated rewards. Successfully reaching ten consecutive victories grants you the one million Killing Point bonus."
The creature then leaned back in its floating chair.

"Both methods have advantages and disadvantages. Challenging active participants can be extremely rewarding if you target someone with a large accumulated pool of Killing Points. However, such opponents are usually very strong. Starting your own trial is safer, but it requires winning ten consecutive battles."
The strange animal then looked directly at Max.
"So, Max Morgan."
Its golden eyes flashed slightly.
"Would you like to challenge someone currently fighting, or would you like to enter the queue and begin your own Ten Consecutive Victory Trial?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1703: Ten Consecutive Victory Trial
paragraphs: Max did not immediately make a decision after hearing the explanation. Instead, he fell into thought for a few moments while weighing the advantages and disadvantages of both options.

Challenging an active participant certainly sounded tempting. If he chose the right target, he could potentially obtain a large amount of Killing Points from a single victory. However, there was also no guarantee that the participant he challenged would have accumulated enough Killing Points to make the risk worthwhile.

On the other hand, the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial offered a guaranteed reward of one million Killing Points if he could successfully clear all ten battles. Considering that he still needed hundreds of thousands of Killing Points before he could even enter the Genesis Trial, the latter option seemed significantly more attractive.

After thinking for a moment, Max looked at the strange animal and asked, "Suppose I choose the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial. Would I still retain the right to challenge someone currently undergoing their own challenge sequence if I find a suitable target?"
The strange animal immediately shook its head.
"No."
Its answer was direct and decisive.

"The Combat Hall does not permit participants to mix the two paths. Once you choose the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial, you remain bound to that challenge until it concludes through either victory, defeat, or voluntary withdrawal. During that period, you are not permitted to challenge active participants. Similarly, those who choose to hunt active challengers cannot simultaneously register for a Ten Consecutive Victory Trial."

The creature flicked its tail lazily before continuing, "The rules were created specifically to prevent participants from abusing both systems simultaneously. Every participant must choose a single path. Either become a challenger who hunts successful fighters or become a contender seeking the one million Killing Point reward."
Max slowly nodded after hearing the explanation.
The rule actually made sense.
Otherwise, powerful participants would simply farm weaker challengers while also pursuing the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial at the same time, making the entire system unfair.
After understanding the restrictions, Max no longer hesitated.
A faint smile gradually appeared across his face.
"I choose the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial."
The moment he said those words, the strange animal immediately nodded as though expecting that answer.
After all, most ambitious participants eventually made the same choice.
The creature quickly manipulated several glowing screens floating before it before a golden rune suddenly appeared in front of Max.
"Registration confirmed."
The rune slowly merged into Max’s body.
"You have successfully entered the queue for the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial. Please wait for your arena assignment."

The strange animal glanced at him briefly before adding, "A piece of advice. The opponents selected for the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial are the ones who chose to challenge the others who have chosen to undergo ten consecutive victory trials like you. So, don’t be surprised if someone way stronger than you challenge you. They are all here to make sure you lose so that they can get the Killing Points you made so far for themselves."
Max merely smiled.
One million Killing Points.
That was his target.

Compared to the astronomical prices within the Divine Ability Pavilion and the five hundred thousand Killing Points required for the Genesis Trial, the reward offered by the Combat Hall was simply too good to ignore.

As the golden rune settled completely into his body, Max left the registration counter and made his way toward the waiting area designated for participants who had chosen the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial.

The area itself was enormous, large enough to accommodate thousands of challengers at once. Participants from every major race could be seen gathered there. Humans occupied a considerable portion of the crowd while demons and elves were equally common sights.
Everyone present shared the same goal. They all wished to conquer the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial and claim the coveted reward of one million Killing Points.
Because of that, the atmosphere throughout the waiting area felt tense and competitive, as though every person present was silently measuring the strength of everyone around them.

The moment Max arrived, numerous gazes immediately landed upon him. His appearance was recognizable enough that many people identified him almost instantly. Countless participants had heard stories about the genius from the Black Dragon Clan who had taken away the sword of the Sword Sovereign.
"It’s that human who became famous recently."
"Yeah, I heard he had the sword of the Sword Sovereign in his hands."
"So what? He is still to weak to pose a threat to us elves. I people of his race wouldn’t take him seriously here."

For a brief moment, whispers spread through portions of the waiting area as people pointed him out to one another. However, that attention did not last long. The moment they sensed his cultivation at the peak of the Law Awakening Realm, many expressions changed subtly. Some looked disappointed while others openly displayed disdain.

To them, fame was one thing and strength was another. No matter how impressive Max’s achievements sounded, the reality was that his cultivation appeared significantly lower than many of the geniuses gathered here.

The majority of participants present possessed cultivation levels at the peak of Law Refinement Realm, while some even emitted a pressure that suggested they were among the strongest younger generation experts of their respective races.
Compared to them, Max’s cultivation simply did not appear threatening enough to deserve serious consideration.

Max naturally noticed those reactions but paid them no attention whatsoever. He had experienced similar situations countless times throughout his cultivation journey. People constantly underestimated him based on his cultivation level, only to regret it later.

As such, he simply ignored the surrounding gazes and quietly stood among the crowd while observing the battles occurring throughout the Combat Hall. In front of him stood ten gigantic arenas arranged in a circular formation around the center of the hall.

Each arena was protected by powerful barriers that prevented the destruction from spilling outward. The sounds of explosions, cheering crowds, clashing weapons, and battle cries continuously echoed throughout the hall as one fierce battle after another unfolded.

He had experienced similar situations countless times throughout his cultivation journey.
People constantly underestimated him based on his cultivation level, only to regret it later.
As such, he simply ignored the surrounding gazes and quietly stood among the crowd while observing the battles occurring throughout the Combat Hall.
In front of him stood ten gigantic arenas arranged in a circular formation around the center of the hall.
Each arena was protected by powerful barriers that prevented the destruction from spilling outward.
The sounds of explosions, cheering crowds, clashing weapons, and battle cries continuously echoed throughout the hall as one fierce battle after another unfolded.

chapters.title: Chapter 1704: Conspiracy of the Starfall Haven!
paragraphs: At the moment, all ten arenas were occupied. Some battles had only just begun while others appeared to be approaching their conclusions. Every participant present watched the ongoing fights closely, either studying potential future opponents or simply entertaining themselves while waiting for their own turn.
Max himself became somewhat interested as he watched. The quality of the combat here was noticeably higher than what he had seen in the battlefield regions outside.

The participants entering the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial all possessed considerable confidence in their own strength. Because of that, even the weaker battles displayed techniques and abilities that would have easily dominated ordinary geniuses.
It was while Max was observing one of the arenas that a voice suddenly called out from behind him.
"You are Max, right?"

Max turned around calmly and found a young human approaching him. The young man wore dark golden robes embroidered with symbols of war and carried a spear on his back. Unlike many of the others present, his expression did not contain the slightest trace of disdain.
"I am Max," Max replied calmly. "And who might you be?"
The young man immediately smiled politely before cupping his fists.
"Please pardon my abrupt approach. My name is Nick and I come from the War God Palace."
The moment Max heard those words, a smile appeared on his face.
"Oh? The War God Palace?"
His impression of the War God Palace was naturally quite positive. Ever since obtaining Saint Reiner’s Saint Token, his status within the War God Palace had become extremely special.
Although he was not an official disciple of the organization, many members treated him with considerable respect because of his connection to one of their Saints.
Nick nodded immediately.
"Yes."
Max’s smile widened slightly.
"No wonder you are being so polite."
Nick laughed awkwardly at those words before glancing toward the arenas.
"Are you also here to participate in the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial?"
"That is the plan," Max replied honestly.
The moment those words left his mouth, Nick’s expression immediately changed.
Max noticed it instantly.
The young man seemed hesitant.
Concerned.
Almost as though he wanted to say something but was uncertain whether he should.
Seeing this, Max frowned slightly.
"What is it?"
Nick looked around cautiously.

His gaze swept across the nearby participants, particularly several demons and elves standing not far away. After confirming that many of them were paying attention to the conversation, his expression became even more serious.
Then, without another word, he switched to Divine Essence Transmission.
His voice sounded directly within Max’s mind.
"There is a very deep conspiracy unfolding within this city."
The sudden statement immediately caught Max’s attention.
The casual expression on his face disappeared.
At the same time, he finally understood why Nick had suddenly become so cautious.
If the matter involved a conspiracy significant enough to warrant secrecy even inside Starfall Haven, then it was clearly not something ordinary.
Max remained outwardly calm, but his interest was thoroughly piqued.
Using Divine Essence Transmission as well, he replied, "A conspiracy?"
Nick nodded subtly.
His expression had become extremely solemn now.
"What conspiracy?"
The moment Max asked that question, Nick’s eyes darkened noticeably, as though merely thinking about the matter was enough to make him uncomfortable.

He remained silent for several moments after hearing Max’s question. His eyes carefully swept across the surroundings once more before he finally continued speaking through Divine Essence Transmission. Judging by his cautious behavior, it was clear that he did not wish for anyone nearby to overhear even a fragment of what he was about to say.
"The conspiracy involves two demons," Nick transmitted. "And they are not ordinary demons."
Max immediately became more attentive.
Nick continued, "Their names are Karo and Munro. Both of them come from one of the strongest first-rate demon forces in the Divine Realm. Their father is a Star Lord."
At those words, Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
He naturally knew what a Star Lord represented.

The Divine Realm was divided into countless star realms, each possessing their own rulers and dominant powers. Those capable of ruling an entire star realm stood at the very pinnacle of existence within that region. Such individuals possessed overwhelming strength, unimaginable influence, and resources beyond the comprehension of ordinary cultivators.
A Star Lord was not simply a title.
It was a symbol of supreme authority.
Nick’s expression grew increasingly grim as he continued.

"Karo and Munro are the sons of that Star Lord. Since entering the Eternal Hourglass, the two of them have been working together. Karo practically lives inside the Combat Hall. He has become infamous among the human participants."
Max remained silent while listening.

Nick continued transmitting, "The way he operates is extremely simple. He does not participate in the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial himself. Instead, he waits. Whenever a human participant reaches eight or nine consecutive victories and is on the verge of obtaining the one-million-Killing-Point reward, Karo immediately challenges them."
A cold light appeared within Nick’s eyes.
"And then he defeats them."
Max immediately understood where this was going.
Nick clenched his fists.
"Every single time."
The frustration in his voice was impossible to hide.

"He defeats them, steals all the Killing Points they accumulated throughout their challenge sequence, and destroys their chance of obtaining the one-million-point reward. He has repeated this process so many times that many human participants have completely lost hope."
Max frowned.
Nick’s expression became even uglier.
"So far, not a single human has successfully completed the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial within Starfall Haven."
The atmosphere around them suddenly felt much heavier.
Max could immediately understand why Nick had referred to it as a conspiracy.
This was not simply bullying.
This was systematic suppression.
Karo was intentionally targeting humans while allowing members of other races to proceed normally.
The result was that human participants continuously lost Killing Points while the demons became increasingly wealthy.
For a few moments, Max remained completely silent.
Then he finally asked a question.
"If things are really as bad as you say, then why do humans continue staying in Starfall Haven?"
Nick blinked.

Max continued calmly, "The main attraction of this city is the Combat Hall. If humans cannot even enjoy the greatest opportunity available here, why not simply leave? The Eternal Hourglass is enormous. There are countless other places where Killing Points can be earned."

chapters.title: Chapter 1705: Elf Race’s Stance!
paragraphs: The moment those words entered Nick’s ears, a bitter smile appeared on his face.
"I thought exactly the same thing when I first arrived here," Nick transmitted through Divine Essence. "And so did many other humans. Unfortunately, that is where the real conspiracy begins."
Max’s expression immediately became more serious.
Nick glanced around once more before continuing.
"Humans did leave Starfall Haven."
His voice gradually became colder.
"At least, they tried to."
Max immediately sensed that something was wrong.

Nick continued, "Most participants are unaware of it when they first arrive, but Starfall Haven has a very peculiar layout. There are numerous ways to enter the city. Participants can arrive from countless different regions throughout the Eternal Hourglass and enter through various gates and pathways. However, there is only one official exit."
Max frowned slightly.
Only one exit?
Nick nodded.
"And that single exit is precisely where the second part of the conspiracy takes place."
The atmosphere around them suddenly became much heavier.
Nick’s expression darkened considerably as he continued speaking.
"Munro."
The name alone seemed to carry immense pressure.
"While Karo remains inside Starfall Haven suppressing human participants within the Combat Hall, Munro stations himself outside the city’s only exit."
Max’s eyes narrowed immediately.
At that moment, he already had a rough idea of what came next.
Nick clenched his fists.
"Whenever a human leaves Starfall Haven carrying a large amount of Killing Points, Munro intercepts them."
His voice carried obvious anger.
"And then he kills them."
A cold silence followed.
Meanwhile, battles continued raging within the nearby arenas while countless participants cheered and shouted, completely unaware of the conversation taking place between Max and Nick.

Nick continued, "At first, people believed it was a coincidence. Then they thought Munro was merely targeting certain individuals. However, after enough incidents occurred, the pattern became impossible to ignore."
His eyes gradually turned colder.
"He specifically targets humans."
Max remained silent.

Nick continued, "Those who lose in the Combat Hall eventually try their luck elsewhere. Those who accumulate Killing Points and wish to leave the city are forced to pass through the exit. And the moment they do, Munro takes everything."
A bitter laugh escaped Nick.
"Karo farms the humans inside Starfall Haven."
"Munro farms the humans outside Starfall Haven."
Max finally understood.
This was far more sinister than he initially imagined.
The two demon brothers had effectively transformed the entire city into a gigantic harvesting ground.
Humans entered the city hoping to earn opportunities.
Inside the Combat Hall, Karo robbed them of their rewards.
If they chose to leave instead, Munro robbed them outside the city.
No matter which path they took, the result remained the same.
The Killing Points eventually flowed into the hands of the two demon brothers.
Nick slowly exhaled before continuing.
"Because of this, many humans now refer to Starfall Haven as a cage."
His eyes slowly swept across the countless human participants gathered throughout the Combat Hall.
"A beautiful cage. Most people trapped inside do not even realize they are being farmed."
Max’s gaze gradually turned colder.
The more he learned about the situation, the more absurd it sounded.
A city created to provide opportunities had effectively become a trap specifically targeting human participants.
Meanwhile, Nick looked directly at Max.
"The worst part is that nobody can stop them. Karo and Munro are already terrifying individually. Together, they are even worse."
A faint look of helplessness appeared on his face.
"Many talented humans have challenged them. Every single one failed."
Then Nick paused briefly before adding one final sentence.
"And because they are the sons of a Star Lord, most people do not dare provoke them even if they survive."
At that moment, Max finally understood why the humans within Starfall Haven looked so frustrated despite having access to one of the greatest opportunities in the Eternal Hourglass.
They were trapped.
And the ones holding the key to the cage were two demon princes named Karo and Munro.

Max remained silent for several moments after hearing Nick’s explanation. His eyes slowly swept across the enormous Combat Hall where countless participants continued cheering, fighting, and gambling away their fortunes without realizing that a far larger game was being played behind the scenes.
After pondering for a moment, Max suddenly thought of another matter.
Since the demons were targeting humans so aggressively, there was still one major race whose position remained unclear.
Turning back toward Nick, Max asked through Divine Essence Transmission, "What about the elves? If the demons are doing this so openly, then surely the elves are affected as well?"
Nick immediately shook his head.
"The elves are different."
His expression became somewhat complicated.

"There seems to be an unspoken understanding between the elves and demons. I would not call them allies because they do not openly cooperate with one another, but they certainly do not interfere with each other’s affairs either."
His gaze briefly shifted toward a group of elves standing near one of the arenas.
Several of them were calmly observing a battle while completely ignoring everything happening around them.
Nick continued, "As far as we can tell, the demons rarely target elves, and the elves rarely provoke the demons. Both sides generally maintain a neutral stance toward one another."
A bitter smile appeared on his face afterward.
"As for what happens to us humans..."
He paused briefly.
"The elves simply do not care."
His voice contained obvious dissatisfaction.

"Whether Karo robs another human inside the Combat Hall or whether Munro kills another human outside the city makes no difference to them. As long as the situation does not affect their own interests, they pretend not to see it."
Nick’s eyes gradually darkened.

"Many human participants originally hoped the elves might oppose the demons since allowing Karo and Munro to grow stronger benefits nobody except the demon race. However, those hopes quickly disappeared."
He looked directly at Max.
"The elves remain completely indifferent."
"Humans lose Killing Points."
"Humans get hunted."
"Humans get trapped inside Starfall Haven."
"They simply watch from the sidelines."
A cold light flashed through Max’s eyes as he listened.

Meanwhile, Nick continued, "In fact, some people suspect that the elves actually prefer the current situation. The demons suppress the humans while the elves remain untouched. Both races continue accumulating resources while the humans become weaker and weaker."
He then shook his head.
"Of course, that is only speculation. Nobody has any proof."
The sounds of cheering suddenly erupted from a nearby arena as another participant was defeated, causing the surrounding crowd to roar with excitement.
Yet despite the noisy atmosphere surrounding them, the conversation between Max and Nick only became heavier.
At that moment, Max’s gaze slowly shifted toward the various elves scattered throughout the Combat Hall.
His expression remained calm.
However, deep within his eyes, a dangerous light briefly flashed before disappearing once again.

chapters.title: Chapter 1706: Nick’s Trust!
paragraphs: After hearing everything regarding Karo, Munro, and the situation of the humans within Starfall Haven, Max remained silent for quite some time. His eyes slowly swept across the enormous Combat Hall where countless battles continued unfolding every moment.

The cheering crowds, the excited participants, and the seemingly peaceful atmosphere all appeared normal on the surface. Yet now that he knew the truth, Max could clearly see the invisible chains binding the human participants.
Whether they stayed within the city or attempted to leave it, they ultimately became prey for the two demon princes.
Eventually, a faint smile appeared across Max’s face.
Through Divine Essence Transmission, he calmly said, "I understand the situation now. Since that is the case, I will take care of the problem here in Starfall Haven myself."
The moment those words entered his ears, Nick’s eyes widened slightly.
He instinctively looked toward Max. For a brief moment, he wondered whether Max truly understood what he was saying.
The opponents in question were not ordinary geniuses. They were the sons of a Star Lord. Even he, a disciple of the War God Palace, couldn’t defeat them.
Among the countless monstrous talents participating in the Cosmic Ascension Conference, Karo and Munro stood near the very top.
Yet despite that, Max’s expression remained completely calm, as though he had merely decided to handle a minor inconvenience.
Nick did not respond immediately.
Instead, he quietly observed Max.
To outsiders, Max’s cultivation at the peak of Law Awakening Realm appeared insignificant compared to the countless peak Law Refinement Realm geniuses gathered within the Combat Hall.
Normally, Nick would never place his hopes on someone with such a cultivation level.
However, Max was different.
Over the past few months, countless stories had circulated throughout portions of the War God Palace regarding the young man standing before him.
Nick personally knew several disciples who had entered the secret domain of Orion alongside Max.
When those disciples returned, they had spoken about him repeatedly.
Some claimed Max possessed combat strength completely detached from his cultivation realm.
Others described impossible battles where Max defeated opponents that should have crushed him easily.
There were even people who claimed that every time Max appeared cornered, he somehow revealed another terrifying trump card that shocked everyone around him.
The more he learned about Max, the more he felt that ordinary logic simply did not apply to him.
And because of that—
He trusted Max should be able to take care of the situation if he said he could do it.

Soon, time gradually passed within the Combat Hall as one participant after another was called from the waiting area where Max stood toward one of the ten massive arenas spread throughout the enormous structure to participate in the ten consecutive victory trial.

This caused the atmosphere to become increasingly lively and intense with every passing minute as countless spectators watched the battles unfold while discussing the strengths and weaknesses of the various challengers, placing bets, exchanging information, and evaluating which participants might have a chance of completing the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial.

Some challengers managed to win their first few battles and returned to the waiting area with renewed confidence, while others suffered immediate defeats and left with bitter expressions after losing everything they had accumulated so far.

Throughout all of this, Max remained calm and patient, silently observing everything around him while occasionally shifting his attention from one arena to another as he studied the participants present within the Combat Hall.

It was during this period of observation that Max finally noticed something unusual. At first, he did not immediately identify Karo because he had never seen him before. However, after watching several battles and paying close attention to the reactions of the crowd, he gradually began to notice a recurring pattern that appeared again and again.

Whenever a human participant managed to reach their eighth or ninth consecutive victory and stood on the verge of obtaining the one-million-Killing-Point reward, a particular demon would suddenly appear and challenge them.

The result of those battles never changed. Every single human who faced that demon ultimately lost, regardless of how strong they had appeared beforehand, and the accumulated Killing Points they had worked so hard to obtain would immediately fall into the hands of that same individual.
Eventually, Max’s attention settled entirely on the demon responsible for those challenges.
That demon was Karo.
The moment Max finally focused on him properly, he immediately understood why Karo had become such a feared figure among the human participants.

The demon’s appearance alone was enough to intimidate most people. He stood nearly three meters tall with a body that looked as though it had been forged from dark crimson metal rather than flesh and blood.
His shoulders were broad enough to make even many demons appear small in comparison, while his arms were covered in dense muscles that radiated explosive strength.
Unlike ordinary demons whose skin was usually black, Karo’s skin possessed a deep crimson color that seemed to glow faintly under the lights of the Combat Hall.

Two enormous golden horns curved backward from his forehead, and strange runes continuously moved across their surfaces like living creatures. His golden eyes were perhaps the most striking feature of all. They contained neither excitement nor anger.
Instead, they held only indifference, as though everyone around him existed on a completely different level from himself.

Strapped across his back was a gigantic black greatsword whose size alone made it appear more like a siege weapon than a personal armament. The sword was almost as tall as Karo himself, yet he carried it effortlessly, casually resting one hand upon its hilt whenever he walked.
Even from a distance, Max could feel a powerful aura radiating from both the demon and the weapon he carried.
However, what truly drew Max’s attention was not Karo’s appearance.
It was the way everyone reacted to him.

Whenever Karo stood up from his seat and began walking toward one of the arenas, the atmosphere throughout the Combat Hall changed instantly. The demon spectators would smile and laugh while openly discussing how many Killing Points Karo was about to acquire.

Meanwhile, the expressions of the human participants would immediately darken. Excitement disappeared. Hope vanished. Many people would lower their heads while others clenched their fists in frustration. It was almost as though they had already accepted the outcome before the battle even began.
Max soon witnessed this phenomenon personally.

Among the countless monstrous talents participating in the Cosmic Ascension Conference, Karo and Munro stood near the very top.
Yet despite that, Max’s expression remained completely calm, as though he had merely decided to handle a minor inconvenience.
Nick did not respond immediately.
Instead, he quietly observed Max.
To outsiders, Max’s cultivation at the peak of Law Awakening Realm appeared insignificant compared to the countless peak Law Refinement Realm geniuses gathered within the Combat Hall.
Normally, Nick would never place his hopes on someone with such a cultivation level.
However, Max was different.
Over the past few months, countless stories had circulated throughout portions of the War God Palace regarding the young man standing before him.
Nick personally knew several disciples who had entered the secret domain of Orion alongside Max.
When those disciples returned, they had spoken about him repeatedly.
Some claimed Max possessed combat strength completely detached from his cultivation realm.
Others described impossible battles where Max defeated opponents that should have crushed him easily.
There were even people who claimed that every time Max appeared cornered, he somehow revealed another terrifying trump card that shocked everyone around him.
The more he learned about Max, the more he felt that ordinary logic simply did not apply to him.
And because of that—
He trusted Max should be able to take care of the situation if he said he could do it.

Soon, time gradually passed within the Combat Hall as one participant after another was called from the waiting area where Max stood toward one of the ten massive arenas spread throughout the enormous structure to participate in the ten consecutive victory trial.

This caused the atmosphere to become increasingly lively and intense with every passing minute as countless spectators watched the battles unfold while discussing the strengths and weaknesses of the various challengers, placing bets, exchanging information, and evaluating which participants might have a chance of completing the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial.

Some challengers managed to win their first few battles and returned to the waiting area with renewed confidence, while others suffered immediate defeats and left with bitter expressions after losing everything they had accumulated so far.

Throughout all of this, Max remained calm and patient, silently observing everything around him while occasionally shifting his attention from one arena to another as he studied the participants present within the Combat Hall.
It was during this period of observation that Max finally noticed something unusual.
At first, he did not immediately identify Karo because he had never seen him before.
However, after watching several battles and paying close attention to the reactions of the crowd, he gradually began to notice a recurring pattern that appeared again and again.

Whenever a human participant managed to reach their eighth or ninth consecutive victory and stood on the verge of obtaining the one-million-Killing-Point reward, a particular demon would suddenly appear and challenge them.
The result of those battles never changed.

Every single human who faced that demon ultimately lost, regardless of how strong they had appeared beforehand, and the accumulated Killing Points they had worked so hard to obtain would immediately fall into the hands of that same individual.
Eventually, Max’s attention settled entirely on the demon responsible for those challenges.
That demon was Karo.
The moment Max finally focused on him properly, he immediately understood why Karo had become such a feared figure among the human participants.
The demon’s appearance alone was enough to intimidate most people.
He stood nearly three meters tall with a body that looked as though it had been forged from dark crimson metal rather than flesh and blood.
His shoulders were broad enough to make even many demons appear small in comparison, while his arms were covered in dense muscles that radiated explosive strength.
Unlike ordinary demons whose skin was usually black, Karo’s skin possessed a deep crimson color that seemed to glow faintly under the lights of the Combat Hall.
Two enormous golden horns curved backward from his forehead, and strange runes continuously moved across their surfaces like living creatures.
His golden eyes were perhaps the most striking feature of all.
They contained neither excitement nor anger.
Instead, they held only indifference, as though everyone around him existed on a completely different level from himself.
Strapped across his back was a gigantic black greatsword whose size alone made it appear more like a siege weapon than a personal armament.
The sword was almost as tall as Karo himself, yet he carried it effortlessly, casually resting one hand upon its hilt whenever he walked.
Even from a distance, Max could feel a powerful aura radiating from both the demon and the weapon he carried.
However, what truly drew Max’s attention was not Karo’s appearance.
It was the way everyone reacted to him.
Whenever Karo stood up from his seat and began walking toward one of the arenas, the atmosphere throughout the Combat Hall changed instantly.
The demon spectators would smile and laugh while openly discussing how many Killing Points Karo was about to acquire.
Meanwhile, the expressions of the human participants would immediately darken.
Excitement disappeared.
Hope vanished.
Many people would lower their heads while others clenched their fists in frustration.
It was almost as though they had already accepted the outcome before the battle even began.
Max soon witnessed this phenomenon personally.

chapters.title: Chapter 1707: Max’s Turn!
paragraphs: One human swordsman fought through nine consecutive battles and finally achieved his ninth victory. The moment he won, loud cheers erupted from the human spectators throughout the Combat Hall because everyone knew he was only one battle away from obtaining the one-million-Killing-Point reward.
Even the swordsman himself appeared excited as he stood proudly within the arena while countless people watched him.
Then Karo stood up.
The cheers immediately died.
The smiles on the faces of many humans disappeared.
A heavy silence spread throughout the surrounding area.
Without saying a single word, Karo calmly walked toward the arena and accepted the challenge.
The battle began.
Three minutes later, it ended.

The swordsman, who had fought through nine difficult battles to reach that point, was killed while Karo stood above him completely unharmed. The accumulated Killing Points instantly transferred to Karo, and the giant demon simply turned around and left without even glancing at his defeated opponent. There was no celebration. No excitement. No arrogance.
To Karo, this appeared to be nothing more than routine.
A simple task he had repeated so many times that it no longer held any meaning.

Watching this scene unfold before his eyes, Max finally understood the extent of the problem within Starfall Haven. This was not merely a strong demon defeating weaker opponents. This was systematic suppression.

Karo was deliberately allowing humans to accumulate Killing Points before taking everything away from them at the last moment, ensuring that no human participant could successfully complete the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial while simultaneously enriching himself through their efforts.

Meanwhile, all around Max, countless human participants watched with expressions filled with anger, helplessness, and frustration. Some openly glared at Karo while others avoided looking at him altogether. Yet despite those emotions, nobody stepped forward to challenge him directly.
The reason was simple.
They were afraid.
Not because of Karo’s status as the son of a Star Lord.
But because of his strength.
And judging from everything Max had seen so far, that fear was not entirely unjustified.

Max continued observing the battles taking place throughout the Combat Hall while occasionally watching Karo, who remained seated in a distant section of the hall like a patient predator waiting for prey to wander into his grasp.
It was at that moment that a beam of golden light descended from above and landed directly upon Nick.
Immediately afterward, a notification appeared above his head.
His turn had arrived.

Nick looked toward the arena assigned to him and slowly exhaled before turning toward Max with a smile. "Looks like it is finally my turn. I will go and see how far I can get. If I am lucky enough to reach the ninth battle, perhaps I will even get the chance to fight Karo myself."
Although he appeared relaxed, Max could easily tell that Nick was not nearly as confident as he pretended to be.
Before Nick could leave, however, Max suddenly spoke.
"Withdraw from the trial."
Nick froze.
For a moment, he simply stared at Max.
Then he frowned slightly and said, "Withdraw? The penalty for abandoning the trial is one thousand Killing Points. That is not exactly a small amount."

Max’s expression remained completely calm as he replied, "One thousand Killing Points is insignificant compared to what you stand to lose. Let me handle Karo. There is no reason for you to throw away all the points you might accumulate during the trial only to have them taken by him in the end."
Nick fell silent afterward.
His gaze instinctively shifted toward the distant figure of Karo, who was currently watching the arenas with the confidence of someone who considered the entire Combat Hall his personal territory.
For several moments, Nick said nothing.

Eventually, he released a long sigh and shook his head helplessly. "Honestly, I do not like this idea at all. Every warrior hates retreating before a battle, especially one that has not even begun yet. However, the more I think about it, the more I realize you are right. Losing one thousand Killing Points is unpleasant, but it is still far better than fighting my way through multiple battles, accumulating tens or even hundreds of thousands of Killing Points, and then handing everything over to Karo at the very end. Compared to that outcome, sacrificing one thousand Killing Points almost feels cheap."
A bitter smile appeared on his face afterward.
Then he looked at Max once more and said, "Fine. I will trust your judgment this time."
With that, Nick headed toward one of the Combat Hall officials and submitted a request to withdraw from the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial.
A few moments later, a notification appeared above him.
[Participant Nick Has Withdrawn From The Ten Consecutive Victory Trial.]
[1,000 Killing Points Deducted.]
Seeing the notification, Nick shook his head once more before returning to Max’s side.
Meanwhile, Max’s gaze slowly drifted toward Karo again.
The giant demon remained completely unaware that someone had just stepped aside because another person intended to deal with him personally.
A faint smile slowly appeared across Max’s face.
Soon enough—
Karo would finally become his problem.
After Nick withdrew from the trial, several other participants went to the arena before finally Max turn came.
A brilliant pillar of golden light descended from high above and landed directly upon Max.
The moment the golden beam appeared, countless eyes within the surrounding area instinctively shifted toward its target.
Participants waiting for their turns, spectators watching the battles, and even some individuals currently fighting in nearby arenas briefly glanced toward the source of the light.
Since everyone present knew what the golden beam represented, they immediately understood that another participant had finally been selected to begin their challenge.
Meanwhile, Max calmly looked upward as the golden light enveloped his entire body.
Several notifications immediately appeared before his eyes.
[Participant Max Morgan]
[Your Turn Has Arrived.]
[Please Proceed To Arena Number 7.]
[Ten Consecutive Victory Trial Beginning.]
[Failure To Arrive Within Five Minutes Will Be Considered A Withdrawal.]
The moment Max read the notifications, a faint smile appeared across his face. He had already spent enough time observing the Combat Hall and learning about its rules.

Now it was finally his turn to step onto the stage and begin earning the Killing Points he needed. More importantly, this would also allow him to personally witness the methods Karo used to suppress the human participants within Starfall Haven.

chapters.title: Chapter 1708: Max’s Arrogance!
paragraphs: Around him, numerous participants immediately recognized his name.
After all, Max Morgan was hardly an unknown figure within the Divine Realm anymore.
Many people had heard about his performance during the Smelting Trial, secret domain of Orion and from the Sword Sovereign’s sword.
Some had even personally witnessed it.
However, the moment their senses swept across his cultivation, many expressions immediately changed.
Some revealed disappointment.
Others showed amusement.
A few even displayed open disdain.

To them, fame and strength were two entirely different things. While Max’s accomplishments had certainly made him famous, his cultivation at the peak of the Law Awakening Realm simply appeared too low compared to the monstrous geniuses gathered within the Combat Hall.
Most participants here stood at the peak of the Law Refinement Realm, and many had already established impressive reputations throughout their respective races.
As a result, whispers immediately spread through the crowd.
"So that is Max Morgan?"
"The one who supposedly dominated the Smelting Trial and defeated Mira, the daughter of the Sword God Palace master?"
"He looks too ordinary."
"Peak Law Awakening Realm? He is too weak in my opinion"
"I expected something more impressive."
"He probably will not even reach the fifth battle."
"Forget the fifth battle. I would be surprised if he survives the third."
Similar discussions continuously echoed throughout the surroundings.
Yet Max completely ignored them.
He had long grown accustomed to people underestimating him based on his cultivation.
If anything, such reactions had become a normal part of his life.
Without wasting another moment, Max calmly stepped forward and began making his way toward Arena Number 7.

As he moved through the enormous Combat Hall, countless gazes followed him. The sea of spectators parted naturally before him while participants standing nearby occasionally glanced toward him with curiosity. Some looked interested while others clearly viewed him as nothing more than another challenger destined to fail.
Meanwhile, Nick silently watched from behind.
Unlike the others, he did not underestimate Max.
After everything he had heard from the disciples of the War God Palace and after personally speaking with Max, he possessed a strange confidence that things would not unfold as everyone expected.
Eventually, Arena Number 7 came into view.
The arena was enormous.

Like the other nine arenas spread throughout the Combat Hall, it was surrounded by powerful barriers designed to contain even the most destructive battles. Countless formations covered its surface while ancient runes continuously glowed along the outer walls.
The fighting platform itself stretched for several kilometers, providing more than enough room for high-level combatants to unleash their full strength without restrictions.
The moment Max arrived before the arena, another notification immediately appeared.
[Participant Max Morgan Has Arrived.]
[Preparing First Battle.]
[Please Enter The Arena.]
Without hesitation, Max stepped forward and passed through the barrier.
The moment his figure entered the arena, a tremendous wave of noise erupted from the surrounding audience.
Cheers.
Shouts.
Discussions.
All of it exploded simultaneously.
Countless spectators immediately focused their attention upon Arena Number 7.
Humans wanted to see whether the famous genius of the Black Dragon Clan could live up to his reputation.
Demons wanted to see how quickly he would fail.
Even many elves shifted their attention toward the arena with curious expressions.
Meanwhile, Max calmly walked toward the center of the massive platform before stopping there.
However, what happened next completely exceeded everyone’s expectations.
Instead of waiting quietly for his first opponent to arrive like every other challenger before him, Max slowly raised his head and swept his gaze across the enormous Combat Hall.

His eyes casually moved across the countless spectators occupying the stands before eventually settling upon the section where the majority of the demons were gathered. For several moments, he simply looked at them in silence. Then, a faint smile slowly appeared on his face.
The smile immediately gave many people a bad feeling.
Then Max spoke.
His voice was calm.
His tone was relaxed.
Yet because of the formations surrounding the arena, every single word echoed clearly throughout the entire Combat Hall.

"Ever since arriving in Starfall Haven, I have continuously heard about how powerful the demon race is. I have listened to endless stories about the so-called genius demons gathered here. Yet after watching for so long, I cannot help but feel somewhat disappointed."

"Aside from Karo, all I have seen are demons hiding behind the reputation of others while bullying weaker opponents. Since there are supposedly so many proud warriors among you, why not stop wasting time and send someone capable of giving me a proper fight? Surely among all the demons present here there must be at least one individual who is not completely useless."
The instant those words finished echoing throughout the Combat Hall, the atmosphere froze.
Complete silence descended.
Even the battles occurring in several nearby arenas seemed less important for a brief moment as countless people stared toward Arena Number 7.
Then—
The silence exploded.
The demon section immediately erupted into chaos.
"What did that human just say?"
"Is he insane?"
"A peak Law Awakening Realm ant dares to speak to us like that?"
"Who gave him the courage to insult the demon race?"
"I will personally tear him apart."
"Forget Karo. I can kill him before he manages to blink."
"Let me enter that arena immediately."

Angry voices continuously echoed throughout the demon section as countless pairs of eyes locked onto Max with undisguised hostility. Many demons had already stood from their seats while glaring toward the arena. Several even released killing intent unconsciously due to their rage.
Meanwhile, the reactions among the humans were completely different.
Many looked shocked.
Others looked excited.
A few even struggled to hide their laughter after witnessing the demons become so furious.
Nick himself stood among the crowd with a strange expression on his face.
Even after everything he had heard about Max, he had not expected him to immediately provoke almost every demon within the Combat Hall.
This was not confidence.
This was blatant arrogance.

Meanwhile, Max simply stood in the center of the arena with a relaxed expression, completely ignoring the furious reactions around him. In fact, when he saw how angry the demons had become, the smile on his face only widened slightly.
Then he spoke again.

"What happened? I thought demons were fearless warriors. Yet all I hear are angry complaints from the audience. If any of you actually possess the strength to back up your pride, then come down here and prove me wrong. Otherwise, sit quietly and continue watching. Your shouting is becoming rather annoying."

chapters.title: Chapter 1709: First Battle!
paragraphs: The moment those words left his mouth, the uproar became even greater than before.
Many demons nearly exploded from anger.
Several powerful demon geniuses immediately rose from their seats.

Even the elves who had previously been observing the situation with indifference now appeared interested. After all, openly provoking an entire race inside the Combat Hall was not something one witnessed every day.
Far away, Karo’s golden eyes slowly narrowed.
For the first time since Max entered the arena, genuine interest appeared on the giant demon’s face.
Most humans who entered the Combat Hall either feared the demons or avoided drawing their attention.
Max had done the exact opposite.
Meanwhile, among the enraged crowd of demons, one individual finally stood up.
The demon was enormous.

Standing nearly two and a half meters tall, his body appeared like a fortress of muscle and steel. Dark gray skin covered every inch of his body while numerous scars crossed his arms and chest, each one evidence of previous battles.
Thick black horns curved upward from his forehead while crimson eyes burned with fury. Resting upon his shoulder was a gigantic warhammer that looked heavy enough to flatten a mountain.
The demon’s expression was incomparably ugly.
Clearly, Max’s words had completely enraged him.
Without saying a single word, he directly jumped from the spectator section.
Boom!
The floor beneath him cracked as he landed heavily before the entrance to Arena Number 7.
The sheer force of the impact caused nearby spectators to take several steps backward.
Then, under the watchful eyes of countless participants, the demon stepped through the barrier and entered the arena.
The moment he arrived inside, a savage smile spread across his face.
His crimson eyes stared directly at Max.
The killing intent within them was so obvious that even the spectators could feel it.
Slowly, the demon lifted the gigantic warhammer from his shoulder before slamming its head against the arena floor.
Boom!
The entire platform trembled violently.
Cracks immediately spread across portions of the arena as a result of the impact.
Then the demon finally spoke.

"Human, since you are so eager to embarrass yourself, I will personally teach you the consequences of insulting the demon race. Remember my name carefully, because it will be the last thing you hear before your defeat. My name is Draven, and I promise you that this battle will end in a single move."
His voice echoed throughout the Combat Hall as confidence radiated from every word.
Around them, countless demons immediately began cheering.
Many already considered the battle finished.
After all, Draven was a peak Law Refinement Realm genius with a considerable reputation inside Starfall Haven.
Meanwhile, standing across from him, Max merely smiled.
There was no tension on his face.
No nervousness.
No concern.
It was as though he was not facing a powerful demon genius at all.
The atmosphere within Arena Number 7 rapidly became increasingly intense as countless spectators focused their attention entirely upon the two figures standing opposite one another.
Max’s first battle in the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial—
Was finally about to begin.
"Now, take my attack!" The demon roared.

The moment those words fell, the demon’s muscles bulged violently, and dark demonic energy surged around his body like a storm. He gripped the handle of his warhammer with both hands, raised it high above his head, and then slammed it down toward Max with terrifying force.
Boom!
The entire arena shook violently the instant the warhammer descended.

The attack had not even fully reached Max yet, but the overwhelming pressure created by the hammer strike had already crushed the air in front of it, causing fierce waves of force to sweep outward in every direction. The stone beneath Max’s feet cracked apart layer by layer while the surrounding battlefield trembled as if it could collapse at any moment.
Many participants watching from outside the arena felt their expressions change.
This demon was not merely relying on a large weapon.
His physical strength was truly terrifying.

The warhammer tore through the air with such brutal power that it seemed capable of smashing a mountain into pieces, and the violent demonic energy wrapped around it made the attack even more frightening. Anyone standing beneath that strike would feel as if the sky itself was falling down upon them.
Yet Max did not move.
He watched the enormous warhammer descend toward him with the same calm expression, and despite the terrifying pressure bearing down on his body.

He did not activate even one of his Seven Divine Veins, nor did he draw upon the power of his Draconic Essences, because in his eyes, this attack was not yet worthy of forcing him to reveal even the smallest part of his true strength.

The demon’s warhammer tore through the air with a horrifying roar, and the force contained within it pressed down like a collapsing mountain, causing the stone arena beneath Max to split apart before the weapon even reached him.

Cracks spread outward like a dense spiderweb, and waves of broken stone were blasted into the air as the overwhelming pressure crashed down upon the battlefield. Many of the watching participants instinctively held their breath, because from their point of view, that strike was powerful enough to smash an ordinary genius into meat paste.
Then, just as the huge warhammer was about to crash into Max’s head, Max slowly raised one hand.
His movement was casual.
It was almost lazy.
The next instant, his palm closed around the head of the descending warhammer.
Boom!
A deafening explosion erupted beneath him.

The entire section of the arena under Max’s feet was instantly obliterated, and countless fragments of stone were sent flying in all directions as the violent force of the demon’s attack poured into the ground.
Dust and debris surged upward like a storm, and the shockwave swept across the battlefield with enough power to make the barriers surrounding the arena tremble faintly.
However, within that ruined crater, Max remained exactly where he had been.
His feet had not moved.
His back had not bent.
His expression had not changed.

He stood amid the shattered arena while holding the demon’s huge warhammer in one hand, and the terrifying weapon that had seemed capable of crushing everything a moment ago now looked like nothing more than a child’s toy trapped in his grip.
For a brief moment, the entire arena fell silent.

Many demons nearly exploded from anger.
Several powerful demon geniuses immediately rose from their seats.

Thick black horns curved upward from his forehead while crimson eyes burned with fury.
Resting upon his shoulder was a gigantic warhammer that looked heavy enough to flatten a mountain.

chapters.title: Chapter 1710: Hundred Thousand KP!
paragraphs: The demon’s crimson eyes widened violently.

His hands were still gripping the handle of the warhammer, and his thick arms were still bulging with strength, but no matter how hard he pushed down, no matter how much demonic energy he poured into his body, the weapon did not move even an inch. It was as if the warhammer had been caught by an immovable divine mountain.
"Impossible," the demon muttered, his arrogant sneer vanishing completely from his face.
That single word came out of his mouth with raw disbelief.
He could not understand it.
He could not accept it.

A human had stopped his full-powered hammer strike with one hand, and this human had done it without releasing any terrifying aura, without revealing any divine power, and without even taking half a step back.
Max looked up at the demon and smiled faintly.
"That is all?"
The demon’s heart trembled the moment he heard those three words.
Before he could react, Max tightened his fingers around the head of the warhammer.
Crack.
A sharp sound echoed through the arena.
The demon’s expression changed instantly.
Crack! Crack! Crack!
More cracks spread across the massive warhammer, and the thick metal surface began to cave inward under Max’s fingers as if it were not forged from powerful demonic iron, but from soft clay.

The demon poured more strength into his arms and tried to pull the weapon back, but the warhammer remained trapped in Max’s hand, unable to move, unable to resist, unable to escape the terrifying pressure crushing it from within.
Then Max applied a little more force.
Bang!
The huge warhammer was crushed apart in his hand.

Fragments of twisted metal burst outward, and the remaining handle shook violently in the demon’s grip before becoming completely useless. The demon staggered backward with a pale face, his hands trembling as he stared at the ruined weapon, and for the first time since entering the arena, real fear appeared in his eyes.
Outside the arena, the watching participants were frozen in place.
The humans stared at Max as if they were seeing a monster hidden beneath human skin.
The demons, who had been laughing and shouting for Max to be smashed to death a moment ago, now stood with stiff expressions, their confidence crushed together with that warhammer.
Even the elves, who usually maintained their elegant calm no matter what happened, could no longer hide the shock in their eyes.
Nick was no exception.
He had always believed that Max would easily take care of the first battle, and he had never doubted that this demon would lose, but even he had not expected Max to be this overwhelming.
He had imagined Max dodging the attack, blocking it with a technique, or perhaps using one of his terrifying powers to suppress the demon, but Max had done none of that.
He had simply raised his hand.
He had grabbed the warhammer.
Then he had crushed it.
Nick stared at Max from outside the arena, his throat moving slightly as he swallowed with difficulty, and even though he knew Max was strong, this scene still shook him beyond belief.
"This guy..." Nick muttered under his breath, his eyes filled with disbelief. "Just how strong is he now?"
Max looked at the demon’s horrified expression and smiled, but that smile did not carry the slightest warmth.
"Now leave behind your Killing Points."

The demon’s body stiffened the moment those words entered his ears, and before he could even recover from the shock of seeing his warhammer crushed like worthless scrap metal, Max’s figure suddenly blurred from where he stood.

There was no loud movement, no visible preparation, and no warning at all. One instant, Max was standing amid the shattered remains of the arena, and in the next instant, he had already appeared directly in front of the demon like a shadow that had crossed space itself.
The demon’s pupils contracted violently.
Too fast.
Max was far too fast.

The demon wanted to retreat, but his body could not respond in time, and the fear that had just taken root in his heart seemed to freeze his limbs in place. The same human he had mocked only moments ago now stood before him like an executioner, and the overwhelming confidence he once carried had been crushed together with his weapon.
Max slowly clenched his fist.

Brilliant star-like radiance erupted from his knuckles, and countless tiny specks of dazzling light gathered around his arm as if a small galaxy had awakened within his flesh. The glow was beautiful, but the power hidden inside it was terrifying, and the moment that stellar energy condensed, the demon felt an indescribable chill rush through his entire body.
"Star Fist."
Max’s voice was calm.
Then his fist drove straight into the demon’s stomach.
Boom!

The impact exploded with terrifying force, and for a brief instant, the demon’s enormous body bent around Max’s fist as if all the strength in his body had been shattered at once. His eyes bulged, his mouth opened soundlessly, and the demonic energy around him collapsed before it could even struggle.
Then the brilliant star-like power erupted from within him, tearing through his flesh, bones, organs, and demonic core in a single devastating burst.
In the next moment, the demon was obliterated completely.
There was no corpse left behind.
There was no final scream.

His huge body vanished into scattered fragments of dark light, and only a flood of Killing Points burst out across the arena like countless blood-red sparks. The number above them was so large that the watching participants felt their hearts tremble.
One hundred thousand Killing Points.
For many participants, that was an amount they could only dream of obtaining after countless battles, but now it had scattered across the battlefield after a single punch from Max.
Max did not waste even a breath.

He raised his hand, and the scattered Killing Points immediately surged toward him like streams of crimson light being pulled by an invisible force. One after another, they entered his body, causing the number beside his name to rise rapidly while the ruined arena around him still echoed with the aftermath of that terrifying punch.
[Killing Points +100,000]
[Current Killing Points: 210,000]
In the Combat Hall, if one got killed by other participants in the arena, then they would directly lose all their Killing Points, which was different from normal situations.
Generally, if one were to get killed by another, they would only lose half the killing points at first, but here that rule didn’t apply.
