chapters.title: Chapter 1721: Max’s Arrogant Words!
paragraphs: Inside the shattered arena, the pressure between Max and Karo continued to rise, and although neither of them had made the first move yet, everyone outside the barrier could feel that this battle was completely different from the previous nine.

The earlier opponents had charged at Max with rage, greed, or arrogance, but Karo stood there with a calm smile and a dark, restrained aura that made him seem far more dangerous than all of them combined.

He was not in a hurry to attack. He was not blinded by anger. He looked at Max as if he had already measured the value of the prey before him and was simply deciding how much effort he needed to use to take everything.
Max looked at him for a moment, then slowly rolled his shoulders as the black dragon scales covering his body gave off a faint metallic sound.
"Use your full strength," Max said calmly.
The words were not loud.
But in the quiet Combat Hall, they spread clearly to everyone watching.
For a brief instant, the entire demon side fell silent.
Then many demons widened their eyes, while some immediately showed furious expressions, because those words were not merely arrogant. They were almost insulting.

Karo had entered the arena after Max reached one million Killing Points, and from the way the other demons treated him, anyone could tell that his status and strength were far above the previous challengers.
Yet Max had not asked cautiously. He had not tested him first. He had directly told Karo to use his full strength, as if Karo was the weaker one who needed to prove himself.
Karo’s smile stiffened slightly.
It was a very small change, but Max noticed it.

The dark aura around Karo became colder, and a trace of irritation finally appeared in his crimson eyes. Until now, he had been watching Max with the attitude of someone looking at an entertaining opponent, but Max’s words had touched his pride.
He could accept arrogance from the strong. He could even admire it. But what he hated was when someone acted as if they were already standing above him before the battle had even begun.
"You really are interesting," Karo said slowly, though the amusement in his voice had faded. "But tell me, human, why are you acting as if you are the strongest one here?"
Max looked at him silently.
Karo took one step forward, and the dark demonic energy around his body surged slightly, causing the broken stones near his feet to tremble.

"Only the strongest has the right to ask another person to use their full strength," Karo continued, his voice becoming colder. "Only the one standing above everyone else can speak those words without sounding like a fool. So why are you saying it to me?"
The demons outside the arena immediately became excited again.
"That’s right!"
"Who does this human think he is?"
"He defeated some useless trash and now thinks he can look down on Lord Karo?"
"Karo will make him understand what real strength means!"

The human participants were silent, but their hearts tightened slightly. They had already seen Max display terrifying power, and many of them believed he was monstrously strong, yet Karo’s confidence was not empty either.

The aura around him alone proved that he was not someone who could be compared to the previous demons, and now that Max had provoked him so directly, the tenth battle was bound to become far more dangerous.
Among the elves, the golden-haired prince narrowed his eyes.
He was watching Max’s expression.
He wanted to see whether that arrogance was a mask or true confidence.
Then Max smiled.
No.
He grinned.
It was a wide grin filled with absolute confidence, and there was not the slightest trace of hesitation, caution, or fear in his eyes.
He looked at Karo as if the question itself was amusing, as if Karo had asked something so obvious that answering it almost felt unnecessary.
"Because I am the strongest individual present in the Combat Hall."
The moment those words left Max’s mouth, the entire Combat Hall seemed to freeze.
The demons stared at him in disbelief.
The humans felt their blood boil.
The elves looked at him with solemn and complicated expressions.
Even Karo’s eyes narrowed sharply.

Max stood in the middle of the ruined arena with black dragon scales covering his entire body, his right hand loosely clenched at his side, and his smile filled with such fearless arrogance that for a moment, it felt as if he truly believed every word he had spoken.
No.
It was not belief.
It was certainty.
He was not boasting to intimidate Karo.
He was stating a fact in his own mind.
Karo stared at Max for several breaths, then slowly lowered his head and laughed. The laugh was soft at first, but it gradually became colder, deeper, and far more dangerous.
The dark demonic energy around him began to rise like black smoke from an abyss, and the air inside the arena turned heavy enough that even the barrier seemed to ripple faintly under the pressure.
"The strongest individual in the Combat Tower?" Karo repeated, his smile returning, though this time it carried a sharp killing intent. "Good. Very good."
He raised his eyes and looked directly at Max.
"Then I will personally tear that title from your mouth."
Max’s grin did not fade.
"Try."
The word was simple.
But it struck the entire Combat Hall like a spark falling into a sea of oil.
In the next instant, Karo’s demonic aura erupted, and a dense wave of dark energy rushed out from his body like black smoke bursting from the mouth of an abyss.

The shattered arena trembled beneath him, the broken stones around his feet rose into the air, and the pressure he released was so much stronger than the previous demons that many participants outside the barrier immediately understood why he had been so confident.

Karo was not one of those ordinary challengers who relied on brute force and anger. His power was refined, heavy, and cruelly controlled, and the moment he released it, the atmosphere inside the Combat Hall changed as if a true predator had finally stepped onto the battlefield.
Max stood in front of him without moving, his black dragon scales gleaming coldly under the dark pressure, and the wide grin on his face did not fade even slightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 1722: Karo Attacks!
paragraphs: Karo’s eyes narrowed.
"Let us see how long that expression lasts."
The moment his voice fell, Karo disappeared.

He did not vanish like the earlier speed-based demon, who had relied on blurry afterimages and chaotic movement. Karo’s movement was clean, silent, and almost ghost-like, as if his body had merged with the shadow beneath his feet.

In the next breath, he appeared directly behind Max, his right arm wrapped in dense black demonic energy that twisted into the shape of a clawed beast head. The attack carried a terrifying devouring force, and the instant it descended, the air behind Max collapsed inward as if the beast head wanted to swallow everything in its path.
"Demonic Abyss Claw."
Karo’s claw struck Max’s back.
Boom!
A violent explosion shook the arena, and the beast-shaped demonic energy bit down on Max’s body with enough force to tear apart a mountain of steel.

This was one of the attacks Karo normally used against humans who managed to reach the tenth battle, and in the past, many proud human geniuses had been torn open by this one strike before they even realized he had appeared behind them. Some had lost their protective armor, some had lost half their bodies, and some had died instantly.
But this time, the result was different.
Max did not even turn around.

The Demonic Abyss Claw struck his dragon scales and erupted with terrifying force, but instead of piercing through his body, the beast-shaped energy shattered against his back like a wave crashing against an unshakable cliff.

Black sparks scattered in every direction, the ground beneath Max’s feet cracked apart, and the shockwave swept forward like a storm, yet Max’s body remained completely steady. Not even his shoulders moved.
Karo’s pupils shrank slightly.
Max slowly turned his head and looked over his shoulder.
"Is this the first attack?"
Karo’s expression darkened for the first time.

The demons outside the arena, who had been waiting to see Max’s body torn apart, suddenly fell silent. They knew that attack. They had seen Karo use it before. They knew how many strong humans had died under it. Yet Max had taken it with his back and remained completely unharmed.

Karo pulled his hand back and retreated several steps, but the irritation in his eyes had grown stronger. He raised both arms, and the black demonic energy around him gathered above his head before rapidly condensing into nine rotating spears.

Each spear was covered in dark red runes, and their tips released a piercing aura that made the surrounding air scream. These spears did not rely on simple weight or force. They were made for penetration, and the demonic runes carved across them carried the power to drill through defenses by focusing their strength into a single point.
"Nine Hell Piercing Spears."
Karo waved his hand.
The nine demonic spears shot toward Max at the same time.
They did not fly in a straight path. Instead, they crossed each other in the air, shifted directions several times, and attacked Max from different angles with terrifying speed and precision.

One aimed for his forehead, one for his throat, two for his chest, two for his shoulders, one for his heart, and the remaining two curved toward his legs. The attack was extremely vicious, and each spear released enough piercing force to make even heavily armored participants feel their scalps turn numb.
Max finally raised his hand.
But he still did not use a technique.
He simply clenched his fist and punched forward.
Bang!
The first spear shattered.
His arm moved again.
Bang! Bang! Bang!

The second, third, and fourth spears exploded into fragments of dark energy before they could touch him. Max’s movements were not flashy, but they were terrifyingly precise. Every punch landed directly on the weakest point of a spear, and each impact destroyed the condensed demonic energy with nothing more than raw physical strength.

The remaining spears tried to change direction and strike from his blind spots, but Max’s body shifted slightly, his left hand swept across the air, and three more spears were smashed apart as if they were nothing but fragile branches.
The final two spears reached his chest at the same time.
Max did not block them.
He allowed them to strike him directly.
Clang! Clang!
Two sharp metallic sounds echoed across the arena.

The demonic spears trembled violently, their sharp tips pressing against Max’s black dragon scales, but they could not enter even half an inch. A moment later, cracks spread across their bodies, and both spears shattered into black smoke.
Max looked at Karo and smiled wider.
"Second attack."
Karo’s face became colder.

This time, even the humans watching from outside the arena felt a strange thrill rise in their hearts. Max was not only blocking Karo’s attacks. He was counting them. He was treating Karo’s famous killing moves as if they were test strikes from a sparring partner, and that attitude made the demons feel humiliated while making the humans feel their blood heat with excitement.
Karo’s killing intent finally sharpened.
"Fine," he said coldly. "Then try blocking this."

He raised one hand toward the sky, and the demonic energy around him suddenly changed. It no longer spread outward like smoke, and it no longer gathered into sharp weapons. Instead, it sank downward, pressing against the arena with a terrifying weight.

The space above Max darkened, and a huge demonic palm slowly condensed in the air, its surface covered with ancient-looking marks that seemed to carry the pressure of countless corpses buried beneath a battlefield.
The moment it appeared, the entire arena groaned under the weight, and even the barrier surrounding the battlefield rippled more violently than before.
"Burial Demon Palm."
Karo pushed his hand down.
The massive demonic palm descended toward Max.

This attack was completely different from the first two. The Demonic Abyss Claw was made to tear through the body, and the Nine Hell Piercing Spears were made to pierce through defenses, but the Burial Demon Palm relied on overwhelming suppression.
It crushed everything beneath it with pure demonic pressure, burying the opponent under a force so heavy that their bones, blood, and energy would collapse at the same time.

Against other humans who had reached the tenth battle, Karo usually used this attack to end everything, because once the palm descended, even those who survived were often left kneeling, broken, and unable to fight again.
The demonic palm fell.

It crushed everything beneath it with pure demonic pressure, burying the opponent under a force so heavy that their bones, blood, and energy would collapse at the same time.

Against other humans who had reached the tenth battle, Karo usually used this attack to end everything, because once the palm descended, even those who survived were often left kneeling, broken, and unable to fight again.
The demonic palm fell.

chapters.title: Chapter 1723: Karo’s Pseudo Cosmic Path!
paragraphs: The entire arena sank.

Cracks spread across the ground beneath Max’s feet, and the ruined stones around him were crushed into powder before the attack even landed. The pressure was so overwhelming that many people outside the arena felt their chests tighten despite the barrier separating them from the battlefield.
Nick’s expression changed slightly, and even the golden-haired elven prince narrowed his eyes as he watched how Max would respond.
Max looked up.
Then he laughed.
He bent his knees slightly, clenched his right fist, and punched straight upward.
There was no Star Fist.
There was no Seven Divine Veins.
There was no additional burst of Draconic Essences beyond the physical strength already raging inside his transformed body.
It was only a punch.
A punch backed by a body so terrifyingly strong that it no longer seemed human.
Boom!

Max’s fist collided with the descending demonic palm, and the entire arena shook as if two mountains had smashed into each other. The massive palm stopped in midair for a brief instant, and the ancient marks across its surface flashed violently as Karo poured more demonic energy into it, trying to crush Max beneath its weight.
Max’s grin remained unchanged.
His fist pushed upward.
Crack!
A long crack appeared across the demonic palm.
Karo’s expression changed.
Max stepped forward, his arm muscles tightening beneath the black dragon scales, and with one more burst of raw strength, he punched through the entire Burial Demon Palm.
Bang!
The huge demonic palm exploded above him.

A storm of black energy scattered across the arena, and the pressure that had nearly buried the battlefield vanished in an instant. Broken waves of demonic force swept across Max’s body, but he stood beneath them with his fist still raised, his dragon scales untouched and his gaze locked on Karo.
"Third attack."
Max slowly lowered his fist.
The Combat Hall was completely silent.
Three attacks.
Three powerful attacks that Karo had used many times before to crush humans who had reached the tenth battle.
One had struck Max’s back and failed.
One had surrounded him with nine piercing spears and failed.
One had descended from above with overwhelming suppression and failed.
Max had blocked them all with physical strength alone.

Karo stood opposite him, his face no longer carrying the same casual smile from before. His crimson eyes stared at Max with cold intensity, and the dark aura around his body slowly became deeper, more dangerous, and far more serious.
Max tilted his head slightly and looked at him with that same fearless grin.
"Now," he said, his voice calm but arrogant enough to shake the pride of every demon present, "are you ready to use your real strength? Your Pseudo Cosmic Path?"
The moment those words echoed across Arena Seven, the atmosphere inside the Combat Hall changed once again.

Many demons outside the arena felt their expressions stiffen, because although they knew Karo was terrifyingly strong, very few of them had actually seen him use his Pseudo Cosmic Path with their own eyes.

In the Cosmic Ascension Conference, every participant treated their Pseudo Cosmic Path as one of their greatest trump cards, and unless they were forced into a dangerous situation, most geniuses would never reveal it so early.

After all, this conference was not a single battle. It was a brutal competition filled with monsters from different races, and once a powerful trump card was exposed, others would begin studying it, preparing against it, and looking for weaknesses.
Karo stared at Max for several breaths.
Then he slowly laughed.
The irritation in his eyes did not disappear, but it was gradually covered by something darker and more dangerous. It was not simple anger. It was excitement.
He had entered the arena thinking that Max was only a fat sheep carrying one million Killing Points, but after those three attacks failed, he could no longer see Max as ordinary prey.
This human’s body was absurdly strong, his dragon scales were almost impossible to break, and his confidence was not merely empty arrogance.
For the first time, Karo felt that crushing Max might actually be enjoyable.
"I truly did not expect this," Karo said slowly, his crimson eyes fixed on Max. "I never thought I would have to use my Pseudo Cosmic Path this early in the Cosmic Ascension Conference."
His voice was calm, but every demon outside the arena heard the weight hidden inside his words.
The humans became tense.
The elves focused their gazes.
Nick’s fists tightened again.

Among the elves, the golden-haired elven prince leaned forward slightly, and even the silver-haired elven woman beside him stared at Karo with solemn eyes, because she had already used her own Pseudo Cosmic Path against Max and had been crushed, so she understood very well that if Karo dared to reveal his at this moment, then it meant his path had to be far more terrifying than ordinary comprehension.
Karo’s grin widened.
"But you are worthy," he said. "A human who can block my three attacks with physical strength alone is at least worthy enough to witness my Pseudo Cosmic Path."
As soon as those words fell, the dark demonic energy around Karo disappeared.
It did not scatter.
It did not weaken.
It simply sank into his body in an instant, and for a brief moment, Karo’s aura became completely silent.
That silence was terrifying.
It felt like the moment before a corpse opened its eyes.
Then the arena darkened.

A black-red light spread from beneath Karo’s feet, and in the next breath, countless cracks appeared across the shattered battlefield. From those cracks, thick strands of abyssal mist rose slowly, and within that mist, countless faint silhouettes began to appear.

Some looked like broken warriors. Some looked like beasts. Some looked like demons. Some looked like humans. Their forms were incomplete, their faces were distorted, and their bodies seemed to be made from smoke, blood, resentment, and death.
The air became heavy with despair.
Karo slowly raised both hands.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path," he said softly. "Abyssal Grave of the Fallen."

chapters.title: Chapter 1724: Abyssal Grave of the Fallen!
paragraphs: Boom!
The entire arena trembled.

The black-red mist exploded outward and swallowed everything around him, forming a massive grave-like domain that seemed to drag the battlefield into the depths of an ancient abyss. Tombstones made of condensed demonic energy rose from the ground one after another, each one covered in strange runes that pulsed like bleeding wounds.

The silhouettes within the mist began to move, and every time they shifted, low whispers filled the air, as if countless fallen souls were crying, cursing, and begging from the bottom of a forgotten battlefield.
This was Karo’s Pseudo Cosmic Path.
Abyssal Grave of the Fallen.
It was not a simple demonic technique.

It was a path built from slaughter, resentment, decay, and domination. Every enemy Karo had crushed, every warrior whose will he had broken, and every opponent whose pride had been buried beneath his power had become part of the idea behind this path.
It carried the terrifying concept of turning a battlefield into a grave, turning resistance into despair, and turning the strength of the fallen into nourishment for the one who ruled above them.
The moment the Abyssal Grave of the Fallen fully appeared, the pressure inside the arena rose to a frightening level.

The shattered stones around Max began sinking into the ground as if pulled by invisible hands. The air around him became thick and oppressive, and the black-red mist tried to coil around his body, searching for gaps in his dragon scales as if it wanted to drag him into the grave-like domain and bury him there forever.

The tombstones surrounding Karo released waves of suppressive force, and each wave carried a different kind of pressure. Some attacked the body. Some attacked the spirit. Some attacked the vitality. Some attacked the will.
Outside the arena, many participants felt chills run down their backs.

Even though they were protected by the barrier, they could still feel the terrifying aura of Karo’s Pseudo Cosmic Path. It was not as sharp as the elven woman’s Death Wind, but it was far more oppressive.

The Death Wind wanted to cut and corrode. The Abyssal Grave of the Fallen wanted to bury everything. It wanted to turn the entire arena into a graveyard and make anyone trapped within it feel that every step, every breath, and every heartbeat was being pulled closer to death.
Several humans turned pale.
Some demons began laughing with renewed confidence.
The elves became solemn.
The golden-haired elven prince narrowed his eyes and muttered, "So this is his path."

The silver-haired elven woman beside him felt her expression tighten. Compared to her Death Wind path, Karo’s Pseudo Cosmic Path felt heavier and more complete. It was not necessarily purer, but it carried a much more brutal killing intent, and the way it suppressed the whole battlefield made it extremely difficult for an opponent to fight freely.
Inside the arena, Karo stood at the center of the grave-like domain, surrounded by tombstones, abyssal mist, and countless fallen silhouettes.
His aura had changed completely.
Before, he had looked like a dangerous demon genius.
Now, he looked like the ruler of a battlefield graveyard.
His crimson eyes glowed from within the mist, and his grin became crueler as the fallen silhouettes behind him lowered their heads as if kneeling before him.
"Do you feel it, human?" Karo asked softly. "This is the grave prepared for everyone who thinks they can stand above me."
The black-red mist surged forward.
The tombstones pulsed.
The fallen silhouettes screamed silently.

Max stood within the oppressive domain, and the black dragon scales covering his body reflected the eerie glow of the abyssal grave. The pressure tried to push him down. The mist tried to bury him. The whispers tried to invade his mind.
But Max did not kneel.
He did not retreat.
He did not even stop smiling.
Instead, his grin became wider as he felt the terrifying power pressing toward him from all directions.
"That is more like it," Max said, his voice carrying genuine excitement.
Karo’s eyes sharpened.
Max slowly clenched his fists, and the black dragon scales covering his arms gave off a deep metallic sound as the draconic power inside his body stirred once more.
Max continued, looking straight at Karo through the abyssal mist, "this finally feels like a a good battle!"

Karo’s grin slowly widened when he saw Max still standing calmly inside the Abyssal Grave of the Fallen, and although the human’s confidence irritated him, it also made the killing intent in his heart grow stronger, because the more Max refused to bend beneath his Pseudo Cosmic Path, the more enjoyable it would be to crush him in front of everyone.

The black-red mist around the arena surged violently, the tombstones made from condensed demonic energy trembled one after another, and the countless fallen silhouettes standing within the grave-like domain raised their heads at the same time, their hollow eyes locking onto Max as if they had all received the same command.
"Since you like acting superior so much," Karo said coldly, his voice echoing through the mist like the whisper of a graveyard, "then show me whether you can still keep smiling after this."
The moment his words fell, Karo raised both hands, and the entire Abyssal Grave of the Fallen answered him.
Boom!

The tombstones around the arena shattered at the same time, and the broken fragments did not scatter randomly. Instead, they rose into the air and fused with the black-red mist, gathering into a massive demonic spear above Karo’s head.
The spear was enormous, dark, and covered in countless blood-like runes, while the fallen silhouettes within the domain began to dissolve into streams of resentment that flowed into the weapon.

Every silhouette that entered the spear made its aura grow more terrifying, and in only a few breaths, the spear no longer looked like a simple attack. It looked like the condensed hatred of an entire battlefield, a weapon created to bury the living together with the dead.
"Abyssal Burial Spear."
Karo’s crimson eyes burned with cruel light as he looked at Max.
"This spear contains the suppressive force of my Pseudo Cosmic Path and the resentment of the fallen souls buried within my grave."

chapters.title: Chapter 1725: Releasing the Full Might of 5000 Draconic Essences!
paragraphs: The massive spear trembled in the air, and its pressure descended before the attack itself moved. The ground beneath Max sank instantly, the broken stones around him were crushed into dust, and black-red mist coiled around his legs like countless hands trying to hold him in place.

The Abyssal Grave of the Fallen was not simply strengthening Karo’s attack. It was also suppressing Max’s movement, his aura, his vitality, and even the flow of power within his body, as if the entire domain wanted to pin him down and make him receive the spear like a condemned prisoner waiting for execution.
Outside the arena, many participants felt their faces turn pale.

Even the demons who supported Karo instinctively quieted down, because they could feel that this was no ordinary move. This was a killing attack born from his Pseudo Cosmic Path, a strike that had likely been prepared to destroy other peak geniuses during the later stages of the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
Yet now, because of Max’s arrogance and overwhelming defense, Karo had brought it out during this tenth battle.
The golden-haired elven prince stared at the massive Abyssal Burial Spear without blinking.

The silver-haired elven woman beside him tightened her grip, and a trace of lingering fear appeared in her eyes, because even from outside the barrier, she could sense that if this attack had been aimed at her, her Death Wind Burial Sword would have been shattered before the spear even fully descended.
Nick’s expression became extremely tense.

He had already seen Max perform impossible feats again and again, but the pressure coming from Karo’s attack was different from everything before it. It was heavy, sinister, and suffocating, and even though Nick believed in Max, his instincts still screamed that this spear was dangerous.
Karo looked at Max and sneered.

"Where is your Pseudo Cosmic Path, human?" he asked. "You claimed to be the strongest individual in the Combat Tower. You said I should use my full strength. Now I have shown you my path, so show me yours."
Max raised his head and looked at the massive spear gathering above Karo.
For a moment, he did not speak.
Then he smiled lightly.
"You want to see my Pseudo Cosmic Path?"
Karo’s eyes narrowed. "If you have one."
Max’s smile widened slightly, but his gaze became colder.
"You are not worthy."
The entire Combat Hall seemed to fall silent.
Karo’s expression froze.
Max continued, his voice calm and direct, as if he was not insulting Karo but merely stating something obvious.
"You are not strong enough to see it."
Those words struck Karo harder than any attack could have.

The black-red mist around him erupted violently, and the Abyssal Burial Spear above his head released a terrifying scream as more and more resentment poured into it. His crimson eyes became icy with killing intent, and the faint grin on his face disappeared completely. Until now, he had been angry and irritated, but this was the first time Max had truly enraged him.
"You will regret those words," Karo said, his voice low and murderous.
Max did not bother answering him.
Instead, he slowly clenched both fists.
The next instant, the power inside Max’s body changed.

Until now, even though Max had used Dragon Scales Transformation and even released the strength of one thousand Draconic Essences earlier, he had still been suppressing the true depth of his physical power.

The strength slumbering inside him had not been fully awakened. The draconic essence within his body had only been partially stirred. But now, as Karo’s Abyssal Burial Spear prepared to descend, Max finally loosened the restraint he had placed upon himself.
Boom!
The full might of five thousand Draconic Essences erupted inside his body.
It was not a simple increase in strength.

It was an explosion of pure draconic force so overwhelming that the entire arena seemed to shake under the weight of his existence. Max’s blood roared like a thousand rivers of molten thunder, his bones released deep cracking sounds like ancient gates being forced open, and the black dragon scales covering his body began to shine with a darker and more terrifying light.

Each scale seemed to awaken completely, and the chaotic patterns moving across them became brighter, deeper, and more alive, as if countless black dragons were swimming beneath the surface of his skin.
The air around Max collapsed outward.
The black-red mist trying to coil around his body was torn apart instantly.
The suppressive force of the Abyssal Grave of the Fallen, which had been trying to bury him beneath its pressure, was violently pushed back by the sheer brutality of his physical aura.

The tombstone fragments floating in the air began trembling, the fallen silhouettes around Karo flickered wildly, and even the massive Abyssal Burial Spear above him shook as if it had suddenly sensed an existence far more ferocious than itself awakening below.
The Combat Hall trembled.

The barrier around Arena Seven rippled again and again, and faint cracks of light began spreading across its surface as if the protection itself was struggling to contain the monstrous pressure erupting from Max’s body.

The participants outside the arena instinctively stepped back. Some weaker humans felt their legs soften. Several demons who had been laughing moments ago turned silent with stiff faces. Even the elves, who usually maintained their composure, looked shaken as the invisible weight of Max’s unleashed draconic power pressed against their senses.
This was no longer the aura of a genius.
This was the aura of a calamity.

Max stood at the center of the destroyed arena, covered in black dragon scales, with five thousand Draconic Essences raging through his body like five thousand furious dragons roaring in unison. The ground beneath his feet could no longer bear the pressure and collapsed downward, forming a deeper crater around him.
Every breath he took caused the surrounding air to tremble, and every slight movement of his fingers released a faint shockwave that scattered the deathly mist nearby.
Karo’s eyes widened despite himself.
For the first time since entering the arena, his confidence wavered.
He had expected Max to be strong.
He had expected Max to have hidden power.
But he had not expected this.

The raw physical strength now erupting from Max was so monstrous that it made his Abyssal Grave of the Fallen feel pressured, and that was something Karo had never imagined happening against a human who had not even revealed his Pseudo Cosmic Path.

Until now, he had been angry and irritated, but this was the first time Max had truly enraged him.
"You will regret those words," Karo said, his voice low and murderous.
Max did not bother answering him.
Instead, he slowly clenched both fists.
The next instant, the power inside Max’s body changed.

Until now, even though Max had used Dragon Scales Transformation and even released the strength of one thousand Draconic Essences earlier, he had still been suppressing the true depth of his physical power.
The strength slumbering inside him had not been fully awakened.
The draconic essence within his body had only been partially stirred.
But now, as Karo’s Abyssal Burial Spear prepared to descend, Max finally loosened the restraint he had placed upon himself.
Boom!
The full might of five thousand Draconic Essences erupted inside his body.
It was not a simple increase in strength.
It was an explosion of pure draconic force so overwhelming that the entire arena seemed to shake under the weight of his existence.

Max’s blood roared like a thousand rivers of molten thunder, his bones released deep cracking sounds like ancient gates being forced open, and the black dragon scales covering his body began to shine with a darker and more terrifying light.

Each scale seemed to awaken completely, and the chaotic patterns moving across them became brighter, deeper, and more alive, as if countless black dragons were swimming beneath the surface of his skin.
The air around Max collapsed outward.
The black-red mist trying to coil around his body was torn apart instantly.
The suppressive force of the Abyssal Grave of the Fallen, which had been trying to bury him beneath its pressure, was violently pushed back by the sheer brutality of his physical aura.

The tombstone fragments floating in the air began trembling, the fallen silhouettes around Karo flickered wildly, and even the massive Abyssal Burial Spear above him shook as if it had suddenly sensed an existence far more ferocious than itself awakening below.
The Combat Hall trembled.

The barrier around Arena Seven rippled again and again, and faint cracks of light began spreading across its surface as if the protection itself was struggling to contain the monstrous pressure erupting from Max’s body.
The participants outside the arena instinctively stepped back.
Some weaker humans felt their legs soften.
Several demons who had been laughing moments ago turned silent with stiff faces.
Even the elves, who usually maintained their composure, looked shaken as the invisible weight of Max’s unleashed draconic power pressed against their senses.
This was no longer the aura of a genius.
This was the aura of a calamity.
Max stood at the center of the destroyed arena, covered in black dragon scales, with five thousand Draconic Essences raging through his body like five thousand furious dragons roaring in unison.
The ground beneath his feet could no longer bear the pressure and collapsed downward, forming a deeper crater around him.
Every breath he took caused the surrounding air to tremble, and every slight movement of his fingers released a faint shockwave that scattered the deathly mist nearby.
Karo’s eyes widened despite himself.
For the first time since entering the arena, his confidence wavered.
He had expected Max to be strong.
He had expected Max to have hidden power.
But he had not expected this.

The raw physical strength now erupting from Max was so monstrous that it made his Abyssal Grave of the Fallen feel pressured, and that was something Karo had never imagined happening against a human who had not even revealed his Pseudo Cosmic Path.

chapters.title: Chapter 1726: Karo’s Panick!
paragraphs: Max slowly raised his gaze and looked at Karo through the storm of black-red mist and draconic pressure.
His smile returned.
But this time, it looked far more dangerous than before.
"You wanted me to reveal my path," Max said calmly, his voice carrying through the trembling arena. "But for someone like you, this is enough."
Karo’s face twisted with fury.
Above him, the Abyssal Burial Spear finally finished forming, and the massive weapon released a world-burying pressure as it pointed straight toward Max.
"Die!"
Karo pushed both hands down.
The Abyssal Burial Spear descended.
At the same time, Max stepped forward.
The entire arena cracked beneath that single step.

The Abyssal Burial Spear descended with world-burying pressure, and as it fell, the entire Abyssal Grave of the Fallen seemed to move with it. The black-red mist roared upward like a sea of death, the broken tombstones released waves of suppressive force, and the countless fallen silhouettes dissolved into the spear one after another, causing its aura to become heavier, darker, and far more terrifying with every passing instant.

It was no longer merely an attack thrown by Karo. It was the full wrath of his Pseudo Cosmic Path, a strike created to bury Max beneath the resentment of the dead and crush his body, spirit, vitality, and will in one blow.
Yet Max only stepped forward.
The arena cracked beneath his foot.
Then his right fist clenched.

Brilliant star-like radiance erupted around his knuckles, and five blazing star marks appeared within the light, each one spinning with terrifying force as if five miniature stars had been compressed into his fist.

At the same time, the full power of his five thousand Draconic Essences raged through his body without the slightest suppression, causing his black dragon scales to shine with a deep chaotic light, while the sound of roaring dragons seemed to echo from within his flesh.

His blood boiled like molten thunder, his bones trembled with overwhelming strength, and the power gathering in his fist became so monstrous that even the air around his arm began to collapse and twist.
Star Fist.
Power of five stars.
Full release of five thousand Draconic Essences.
The moment these two forces fused together, the entire Combat Hall seemed to lose its sound.
Even Karo’s expression changed.
For the first time, his eyes showed true fear.
He could feel it clearly now. The power gathering in Max’s fist was not something his Abyssal Burial Spear could easily suppress.

It was violent, pure, and unbelievably heavy, and when that draconic strength merged with the five-star power, it felt as if Max was not preparing to punch with a human fist, but with the crushing weight of five stars and the combined rage of five thousand dragons.
"No..." Karo muttered instinctively, but the word barely left his mouth before Max moved.
Max punched forward.
Boom!

The five-star radiance shot upward like a blazing celestial pillar, and the draconic power inside it roared with enough force to shake the entire arena. The fist light collided head-on with the Abyssal Burial Spear, and for a single instant, the spear seemed to stop in midair.

Black-red energy and starry light crashed against each other, deathly mist and chaotic draconic pressure tore through the battlefield, and the shockwave that erupted from their collision slammed into the barrier so fiercely that countless ripples spread across its surface.
Karo gritted his teeth and poured everything into his Pseudo Cosmic Path.

The Abyssal Grave of the Fallen trembled violently, and every remaining tombstone shattered at once, transforming into more abyssal force that surged into the spear. The fallen silhouettes screamed without sound, and their resentment poured into the attack like fuel thrown into a dying flame.
Karo’s crimson eyes became bloodshot as he tried to force the spear downward, desperate to bury Max beneath the full might of his path.
But Max’s fist did not retreat.
It rose.
One inch.
Then another.
Crack!
A sharp sound echoed from the Abyssal Burial Spear.
Karo’s pupils contracted.

A long crack appeared across the body of the massive spear, and from that crack, brilliant star-like light burst outward like dawn tearing through a grave. The black-red runes covering the spear flickered wildly, but they could not withstand the force pressing against them.

Max’s five-star fist power crushed forward, and the strength of five thousand Draconic Essences surged behind it like an endless tide, pushing through the spear’s suppressive power with brutal and unstoppable force.
Crack! Crack! Crack!
More cracks spread across the Abyssal Burial Spear.

The enormous weapon that had carried the resentment of the fallen and the pressure of Karo’s Pseudo Cosmic Path began to break apart under Max’s punch. Its tip shattered first, then the shaft split open, then the blood-red runes collapsed one after another, and the countless fallen silhouettes trapped within the spear were torn apart by the blazing star radiance before they could even struggle.
Karo’s face twisted in disbelief.
"Impossible!"
Max’s eyes remained cold.
His fist pushed forward completely.
Bang!
The Abyssal Burial Spear exploded.
A storm of black-red energy burst across the arena, but before it could spread, Max’s fist light tore through it and continued forward. The five-star radiance did not stop after destroying the spear.
It rushed straight into the heart of the Abyssal Grave of the Fallen, smashing through the black-red mist, shattering the remaining tombstones, and crushing the grave-like domain from the inside out.
The entire Pseudo Cosmic Path began to collapse.
The battlefield graveyard that Karo had summoned trembled violently, and the abyssal mist that had swallowed the arena was ripped apart by Max’s draconic pressure. Tombstones cracked and vanished.

Fallen silhouettes screamed and dissolved. The suppressive force that had tried to bury everything broke apart like rotten wood beneath a hammer. In only a few breaths, the terrifying Abyssal Grave of the Fallen, which had made humans, demons, and elves feel chills across their backs, was being destroyed by the raw, overwhelming might of Max’s fist.
Karo staggered backward.
Blood burst from his mouth.

His Pseudo Cosmic Path was connected to his power, his will, and his foundation. The moment Max began crushing it, the backlash struck him like a mountain collapsing onto his soul. His body trembled, his aura became chaotic, and the confident demon who had entered the arena to steal one million Killing Points finally looked as if he had seen something beyond his understanding.
Max stepped forward again.
His fist light pierced through the final layer of the Abyssal Grave of the Fallen.
Bang!
The grave-like domain shattered completely.
The black-red mist vanished.
The tombstones disappeared.
The fallen silhouettes were annihilated.
Karo’s Pseudo Cosmic Path was destroyed in front of everyone.
The Combat Hall fell into deathly silence.
Then Max appeared before Karo.
There was no warning.
There was no chance to dodge.
Karo had barely raised his head when Max’s fist, still burning with five-star radiance and the terrifying power of five thousand Draconic Essences, arrived in front of his chest.
For the first time, Karo’s face showed panic.
"Wait..."
Max’s expression did not change.
His fist landed.
Boom!

Karo’s body bent violently around the impact, and the remaining demonic energy protecting him shattered instantly. The five-star power erupted through his body, while the force of five thousand Draconic Essences crushed his bones, organs, and demonic core in the same breath.
His crimson eyes widened, his mouth opened, and the arrogance that had been carved into his face since the beginning vanished completely beneath the overwhelming force of Max’s punch.
Then his body exploded into nothingness.
There was no final roar.
There was no chance to resist.

Karo, the demon who had waited until Max gathered one million Killing Points, the demon who had revealed his Pseudo Cosmic Path and tried to bury Max beneath the Abyssal Grave of the Fallen, was obliterated by a single punch.
The moment he died, an enormous amount of crimson light erupted across the arena.

His Killing Points scattered like a storm of blood-red stars, filling the shattered battlefield with dazzling radiance. The amount was far greater than any opponent Max had defeated so far, and the display above the arena flickered violently as the trial recognized the end of the tenth battle.

chapters.title: Chapter 1727 - 8 Million Killing Points!
paragraphs: Max stood alone in the center of the destroyed arena.
His black dragon scales gleamed.
His right fist slowly lowered.
The remnants of star radiance faded around his hand, while the monstrous power of five thousand Draconic Essences still raged inside his body like dragons unwilling to return to sleep.
Outside the arena, no one spoke.
The demons stared blankly at the place where Karo had vanished, their faces pale and frozen with disbelief.
The humans looked at Max as if they were seeing a legend being born before their eyes.
The elves remained silent, but their gazes had changed completely.

Among them, the golden-haired elven prince’s expression was no longer calm. His emerald eyes were fixed on Max, and the familiar feeling in his heart had now turned into something close to certainty, though that certainty also brought a trace of deep unease.
Nick swallowed with difficulty.
He had believed Max was strong.
But this was no longer simply strong.
Max had destroyed Karo’s strongest attack, shattered his Pseudo Cosmic Path, and killed him in one punch.
Inside the arena, Max raised his hand, and the countless Killing Points left behind by Karo surged toward him like a crimson tide.
He absorbed them all without hesitation.
Then he looked at the empty space where Karo had stood and smiled faintly.
"You wanted my one million Killing Points," Max said softly. "In the end, you only delivered yours."
The moment Karo’s body was obliterated, the entire ruined arena was drowned in crimson light.
It was not like the previous opponents.

When the other demons and the elven woman had died, their Killing Points had scattered like bright streams or small storms of blood-red sparks, but the amount released from Karo was on an entirely different level.

The crimson radiance that burst out from where his body had vanished spread across the arena like a sea of blood-colored stars, filling the shattered battlefield with so much light that even the black dragon scales covering Max’s body were dyed in a deep red glow.
Countless streams of Killing Points floated in the air, dense, dazzling, and overwhelming, and for a moment, the entire Combat Hall felt as if it had fallen beneath a crimson sky.
The display above the arena flickered violently.
Then Karo’s total appeared for everyone to see.
[Defeated Participant: Karo]
[Killing Points: 6,000,000]
The moment that number appeared, the Combat Hall fell into a silence so deep that even breathing seemed to stop.
Six million Killing Points.
Karo had possessed six million Killing Points.

That amount was enough to make countless participants risk their lives, enough to make demons betray one another, enough to make humans and elves feel their hearts tremble with greed and fear at the same time.

It was not the kind of number an ordinary participant could gather through a few lucky battles. It represented slaughter, domination, and the defeat of many powerful opponents before he had ever stepped into Arena Seven.
Yet now, all of it belonged to Max.
The trial’s rules activated instantly.

The crimson sea of Killing Points surged toward Max from every direction, rushing into his body like countless rivers returning to an endless ocean. One stream after another poured into him, wrapping around his dragon-scaled figure before disappearing into his body, and with every passing breath, the number beside his name began rising at a terrifying speed.
The Combat Hall’s display flashed again and again, unable to hide the absurd increase as Karo’s six million points were absorbed completely.
[Participant: Max]
[Consecutive Victories: 10]
[Previous Killing Points: 1,000,000]
[Absorbed Killing Points: 6,000,000]
[Current Killing Points: 7,000,000]
[Participant Max Morgan is awarded 1,000,000 KP for completing the Ten Consecutive Victory Trial.]
[Current Killing Points: 8,000,000]
The moment the final number appeared, a heavy pressure seemed to descend upon everyone present.
Eight million Killing Points.

Max had entered the tenth battle with one million Killing Points, and after killing Karo, that number had skyrocketed to eight million in an instant. The total was so outrageous that many participants could only stare at the display with blank expressions, unable to process what they were seeing.

A human who had just completed the ten consecutive victory trial had not only survived Karo’s Pseudo Cosmic Path, but had crushed it, killed him, and taken all six million Killing Points he had accumulated.
The demons looked as if their souls had been struck.
Some stared at the empty place where Karo had vanished, their faces pale with disbelief, while others looked at Max with fear that they could no longer hide. Karo had not been a nameless demon.

He had been someone strong enough to make them confident, someone they believed could end Max’s arrogance, someone who had carried six million Killing Points as proof of his dominance. But now, Karo was gone, and the proof of his strength had become Max’s reward.
The humans, on the other hand, felt their blood burn.

Several of them clenched their fists so hard their knuckles turned white, their eyes fixed on Max as if they were witnessing something that would be spoken of long after this trial ended. Nine victories had already made him terrifying. Killing Karo made him monstrous.
But reaching eight million Killing Points after completing the tenth battle made him something else entirely.
A calamity.
A legend.
A human genius who had stepped over demons and elves alike in front of the entire Combat Hall.

Among the elves, the golden-haired elven prince stared at the number above Max with narrowed eyes, but this time, even he could not maintain his earlier calm completely. eight million Killing Points was not the only thing that mattered.

What mattered more was how Max had obtained them. He had destroyed the Abyssal Grave of the Fallen without revealing his own Pseudo Cosmic Path, and he had killed Karo using only his Dragon Scales Transformation, his five-star Star Fist, and the full might of five thousand Draconic Essences.
That meant Max was still hiding something.
The silver-haired elven woman beside the prince also stared at Max in silence, and the memory of being obliterated by his fist returned to her mind with uncomfortable clarity.
She now understood that when Max had fought her, he truly had held back. If he had used the same power against her that he had used against Karo, there would not have even been a clash.
Inside the arena, Max slowly lowered his hand after absorbing the last stream of crimson light.

The monstrous power of five thousand Draconic Essences still raged inside him, but his expression remained calm, almost relaxed, as if killing Karo and gaining six million Killing Points had only been a natural outcome.
The black dragon scales covering his body gleamed under the fading crimson radiance, and the ruined arena beneath his feet looked like it had been crushed by the landing of an ancient beast.
Then a notification appeared before his eyes.
[Ten Consecutive Victory Trial Completed]
[Victories: 10]
[Final Killing Points: 8,000,000]
[Trial Result: Perfect Completion]
Max looked at the notification for a moment.
Then he smiled faintly.
"Eight Million points is nice."
His voice was not loud, but in the silent Combat Hall, many participants heard it clearly.
The demons felt their faces burn with humiliation.
The humans almost laughed aloud.
Nick stared at Max with wide eyes, then slowly exhaled as if he had only just remembered how to breathe.
"Eight million..." Nick muttered under his breath, his voice filled with disbelief. "He actually reached eight million Killing Points in one trial."
Max raised his eyes and swept his gaze across the Combat Hall.
This time, no demon dared to mock him.
No elf dared to underestimate him.
No human dared to think his arrogance was empty.
He had stood in Arena Seven, taken ten consecutive battles, killed Karo, shattered a Pseudo Cosmic Path, and walked out with eight million Killing Points.
At that moment, everyone understood one thing.
The name Max had truly entered the sight of every race present in the Combat Tower.

Killing Karo made him monstrous.
But reaching eight million Killing Points after completing the tenth battle made him something else entirely.
A calamity.
A legend.
A human genius who had stepped over demons and elves alike in front of the entire Combat Hall.

Among the elves, the golden-haired elven prince stared at the number above Max with narrowed eyes, but this time, even he could not maintain his earlier calm completely. eight million Killing Points was not the only thing that mattered.
What mattered more was how Max had obtained them.

He had destroyed the Abyssal Grave of the Fallen without revealing his own Pseudo Cosmic Path, and he had killed Karo using only his Dragon Scales Transformation, his five-star Star Fist, and the full might of five thousand Draconic Essences.
That meant Max was still hiding something.
The silver-haired elven woman beside the prince also stared at Max in silence, and the memory of being obliterated by his fist returned to her mind with uncomfortable clarity.
She now understood that when Max had fought her, he truly had held back.
If he had used the same power against her that he had used against Karo, there would not have even been a clash.
Inside the arena, Max slowly lowered his hand after absorbing the last stream of crimson light.

The monstrous power of five thousand Draconic Essences still raged inside him, but his expression remained calm, almost relaxed, as if killing Karo and gaining six million Killing Points had only been a natural outcome.
The black dragon scales covering his body gleamed under the fading crimson radiance, and the ruined arena beneath his feet looked like it had been crushed by the landing of an ancient beast.
Then a notification appeared before his eyes.
[Ten Consecutive Victory Trial Completed]
[Victories: 10]
[Final Killing Points: 8,000,000]
[Trial Result: Perfect Completion]
Max looked at the notification for a moment.
Then he smiled faintly.
"Eight Million points is nice."
His voice was not loud, but in the silent Combat Hall, many participants heard it clearly.
The demons felt their faces burn with humiliation.
The humans almost laughed aloud.
Nick stared at Max with wide eyes, then slowly exhaled as if he had only just remembered how to breathe.
"Eight million..." Nick muttered under his breath, his voice filled with disbelief.
"He actually reached eight million Killing Points in one trial."
Max raised his eyes and swept his gaze across the Combat Hall.
This time, no demon dared to mock him.
No elf dared to underestimate him.
No human dared to think his arrogance was empty.
He had stood in Arena Seven, taken ten consecutive battles, killed Karo, shattered a Pseudo Cosmic Path, and walked out with eight million Killing Points.
At that moment, everyone understood one thing.
The name Max had truly entered the sight of every race present in the Combat Tower.

chapters.title: Chapter 1728: Karo went into Hiding!
paragraphs: After the final notification faded from his vision, Max remained standing in the center of the destroyed arena for a few more moments, allowing the last traces of crimson light to disappear into his body while the number of eight million Killing Points still lingered above him like a declaration no one in the Combat Hall could ignore.

The barrier around Arena Seven slowly opened, and only then did Max loosen the power raging inside him, letting the full might of five thousand Draconic Essences settle back into the depths of his body while the black dragon scales covering him gradually lost some of their overwhelming pressure, though they did not disappear completely.
He stepped down from the arena.

The moment his foot touched the ground outside the battlefield, many participants instinctively moved away from him. It was not because Max had released any killing intent toward them, and it was not because he had said anything threatening.

It was simply because they had all seen what had happened inside the arena. They had seen demons crushed with bare fists, an elf genius obliterated by Star Fist, and Karo’s Pseudo Cosmic Path shattered completely before he himself was killed in one punch. After witnessing all of that, no one could look at Max as an ordinary participant anymore.
Max ignored their reactions.
His gaze moved across the Combat Hall.
He was looking for Karo.

Although he had killed Karo in the tenth battle, Max did not believe that the demon had been completely eliminated from the Eternal Hourglass. Just like the silver-haired elven woman had reappeared after being killed, Karo should still have more lives left.
If Max guessed correctly, Karo should have three more lives, which meant the demon should have revived somewhere inside the Combat Hall after paying the price of death.
But after scanning the demon side, Max did not see him.

He looked across the corners of the hall, toward the shadowed areas where some participants stood silently, toward the groups of demons who had gathered together, and even toward the distant exits leading away from the Combat Hall, but Karo was nowhere to be found.
The demons who had once stood proudly around him now looked tense and uneasy, and none of them dared to meet Max’s gaze for long.
A faint sneer appeared on Max’s face.
"So he is hiding really well."
His voice was soft, but the mockery in it was clear.

Karo had entered the arena with confidence, waited for Max to gather one million Killing Points, and acted as if everything Max possessed already belonged to him. Yet after being killed once, he had vanished so quickly that Max could not even find his shadow in the Combat Hall. The thought made Max’s smile turn colder.
"Then he should keep hiding well," Max muttered, his eyes narrowing slightly as he glanced once more across the demon side. "Because if I see him again, I will kill him again."
The demons who heard those words felt their expressions stiffen.
No one dared to respond.

If another human had said such a thing after killing Karo once, the demons would have erupted in fury and ridicule. But when Max said it while standing there with eight million Killing Points, black dragon scales still covering parts of his body, and the pressure of his previous battle still lingering around him, even the most arrogant demons could only swallow their anger in silence.
Thinking along those lines, Max finally withdrew his gaze and walked back toward Nick.
The crowd parted wherever he went.

Some humans looked at him with bright eyes filled with admiration, while a few even seemed to want to speak, but none of them found the courage to step forward first. The elves watched him with complicated expressions, especially the golden-haired elven prince, whose gaze followed Max’s figure with silent intensity.
The demons, on the other hand, looked at him with resentment, fear, and humiliation, but after what had happened to Karo, none of them dared to challenge him casually.
Nick was already waiting for him.

The moment Max approached, Nick’s tense expression broke into a wide smile, and the shock in his eyes finally gave way to excitement that he could no longer suppress. He looked at Max as if he was seeing him properly for the first time, and although he had always believed Max was strong, the ten consecutive victory trial had completely shattered his previous understanding of that strength.
"You really did it," Nick said, his smile widening even more. "Ten consecutive victories, eight million Killing Points, and you even killed Karo in front of everyone."
Max looked at him and smiled faintly.
"That demon wanted my points," Max said casually. "So I took his instead. Besides, I already told you I would take care of him."
Nick stared at him for a second, then laughed under his breath.
Only Max could say something like that so casually after shaking the entire Combat Hall.

Behind them, the display above Arena Seven still showed Max’s final result, and even though the trial had ended, many participants continued staring at the number as if they wanted to carve it into their memories.
[Participant: Max]
[Ten Consecutive Victory Trial Completed]
[Final Killing Points: 8,000,000]
Nick looked at the display again, then turned back to Max with a grin that he could not hide.
"Do you even know how insane that number looks?"
Max glanced at the display once, then shrugged lightly.

"It is only the beginning. I still have to kill Karo three more times and then there is also his brother Munro. I have to take care of him too. I believe they would deliver me a good amount of Killing Points for sure."
Nick’s smile froze for a moment.
Then he shook his head and laughed helplessly, because after everything he had just witnessed, he could not even say Max was exaggerating.
Max looked at Nick and said calmly, "I am heading toward the exit of the city."
Nick’s smile faded slightly when he heard that.
"The exit?" he asked. "Already?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1729: Elf Prince’s Approach!
paragraphs: Max nodded, and his expression became a little colder as the name of his next target appeared in his mind. "I still have to take care of Munro. After that, I will be heading somewhere else."
Nick understood immediately.
Munro.

The moment that name appeared, Nick’s expression also turned serious. He had not forgotten the reason Max had entered this place, nor had he forgotten that Max still had enemies waiting outside the Combat Hall.

The trial had given Max an absurd number of Killing Points, but to Max, this was clearly not the end. It was only one stop along the way. There were still matters he had to settle, and knowing Max’s personality, if he said he was going to take care of Munro, then Munro’s fate was already almost decided.
Max placed one hand on Nick’s shoulder and looked at him with a faint smile.
"Take care of yourself," Max said. "Do not get dragged into unnecessary fights, and if someone troublesome comes looking for you, avoid them if you can."
Nick looked at him for a moment, then gave a helpless smile.
"You say that after causing the biggest scene in the entire Combat Hall?"
Max shrugged lightly. "That is different."

Nick almost laughed, but then he sighed and nodded. "Fine. I will be careful. You should also watch yourself. After what you did, demons, elves, and probably even some humans will start paying attention to you."
Max smiled faintly. "Let them."
After saying that, he turned around and prepared to leave.
However, before Max could take more than a few steps, a figure suddenly appeared in front of him and blocked his path.
The surrounding atmosphere changed at once.
The person standing before him was the golden-haired elven prince.

He stood there with calm elegance, his long golden hair falling smoothly over his shoulders, his emerald eyes fixed directly on Max, and his posture carrying the natural nobility of someone who had been born above others.

He did not release any killing intent, nor did he show hostility openly, but the moment he stood in front of Max, many participants nearby instinctively quieted down. Even among the elves, his status was clearly not ordinary.
Standing beside him was the silver-haired elven woman Max had killed not long ago.

Her face was complicated knowing how she had been defeated by Max, but her eyes were calm as she stood slightly behind the golden-haired prince. When she looked at Max again, there was no hatred in her gaze, only caution, curiosity, and a lingering seriousness that had not been there before their battle.
Max stopped.
Nick’s expression immediately changed, and he stepped slightly closer to Max, his eyes moving between the golden-haired elven prince and the silver-haired woman.
The nearby humans also became tense.
The demons watched silently from a distance, some with cold smiles, as if they hoped another conflict would break out before Max could leave the Combat Hall.
Max looked at the golden-haired elven prince, then glanced at the silver-haired woman beside him.
His smile became faintly mocking.
"What is this?" Max asked. "Do the elves want another test?"
The silver-haired elven woman’s expression shifted slightly, but she did not speak.
The golden-haired elven prince looked at Max in silence for a moment, and his gaze seemed to study every part of him.
"No," the golden-haired elven prince said calmly. "I am not here to challenge you."
Max raised an eyebrow.
"Then move."
The words were casual, but they carried enough arrogance to make several elves behind the prince frown.

The golden-haired prince did not seem offended by Max’s cold attitude. He simply stood in front of him with the same calm expression, his emerald eyes studying Max’s face as if he was looking for a reaction that could confirm the suspicion forming in his mind.
"I only want to ask you something," the golden-haired prince said.
Max narrowed his eyes slightly.
"What is it?" he asked, his voice carrying a trace of curiosity despite the impatience in his expression.
The golden-haired prince looked at him for a brief moment, then asked in a casual tone, "Who is Caelira to you?"
The moment that name entered Max’s ears, everything around him seemed to stop.
His expression changed instantly.

The calmness in his eyes shattered, and an uncontrollable surge of rage exploded from deep within his chest. That name was not something he had expected to hear here, not from an elf, and certainly not from someone who looked as young as the golden-haired prince. Caelira was his mother.

Even though Max knew it was the elves who had taken his parents away, he had never thought the younger generation of the elves would know anything related to that incident, because in his mind, something so cruel and secretive should have been hidden among the higher ranks of their race.
But this elf had spoken her name.
He had spoken it casually.
"How do you know that name?!" Max snapped.
The words came out like a roar.

Before anyone nearby could react, Max stepped forward and grabbed the golden-haired prince by the collar. His fingers clenched tightly around the elven prince’s clothes, and a violent wave of energy burst from his body as his emotions tore through the restraint he had placed upon himself. The humans nearby froze in shock.

The elves behind the golden-haired prince immediately moved as if they wanted to act, but the silver-haired elven woman raised one hand and stopped them, her face tense as she stared at Max’s furious expression.
Max did not care about any of them.
His eyes were locked onto the golden-haired prince.

If he had known the younger generation of the elves might possess information about his mother, then his attitude toward them inside the Combat Hall would have been completely different. He might not have simply killed and ignored them.
He might have captured a few, broken their pride, and tortured the answers out of them one by one. The thought alone made the rage inside him burn even hotter.
"Calm down," the golden-haired prince said, his voice still strangely steady despite being held by the collar.

chapters.title: Chapter 1730: Following Golden Elf Prince!
paragraphs: "Calm down?!" Max raged.

The energy in his body erupted even more violently, and black dragon scales began appearing across his skin once again without his conscious command. They spread over his arms, neck, and face, gleaming with a cold chaotic light as his uncontrolled emotional state dragged his bloodline power to the surface.
His pupils sharpened, his fingers tightened, and the air around him trembled under the pressure rolling out from his body.
"If you do not tell me how you know that name," Max said, his voice low and dangerous, "I will make sure you are eliminated right here and now."
The golden-haired prince stared at him without fear, but before he could answer, the energy Max released reached a dangerous peak.
Then, without warning, a beam of white light descended from above and fell directly upon Max.
The light wrapped around his body in an instant.
Max frowned.

The raging energy inside him suddenly disappeared as if it had been sealed by an invisible hand, and the black dragon scales that had begun spreading across his skin stopped growing. His grip on the golden-haired prince weakened slightly, and for a brief moment, Max felt as if all the strength inside his body had been locked away.
He could still stand. He could still move. But the terrifying power that had been surging through him a moment ago was no longer responding to his will.
"What is happening?" Max asked, his voice still filled with anger.
Nick, who had been standing nearby with a solemn expression, immediately stepped forward and said, "Max, it is the rules of Starfall Haven."
Max glanced toward him.

Nick’s expression was serious as he continued, "You cannot use strength or release too much energy inside Starfall Haven. Remember, this is a peaceful city and a neutral zone where killing is prohibited outside the proper battle areas."
Max stared at him for a moment.
Then he slowly took a deep breath.

The rage in his eyes did not disappear, but he forced it down with sheer will. He understood the situation now. Starfall Haven had its own rules, and those rules were not something even he could casually ignore. If he lost control here, the city itself would suppress him before he could act.
"I see," Max said coldly.

He turned back toward the golden-haired prince, released his collar, and stepped back half a pace. The white light around his body gradually faded once his energy settled, but the killing intent in his eyes remained sharp enough to make the nearby elves tense.
Max looked at the golden-haired prince again and asked, each word controlled but heavy with threat, "How do you know that name?"
The golden-haired prince adjusted his collar calmly, then looked at Max with a gaze that had become far more serious than before.
"Come with me," he said.

After saying that, he turned and began walking toward a secluded area of the Combat Hall, one far away from the demons, humans, and most of the elven participants. The silver-haired elven woman followed beside him, but she kept glancing back at Max, clearly aware that one wrong word could make this situation explode again.
Max followed without hesitation.
He did not care whether this was a trap.
He did not care whether the golden-haired prince had some hidden motive.

The moment his mother’s name had been spoken, everything else became secondary. Munro, Karo, the Killing Points, and even the attention of the Combat Hall all faded behind the single question burning inside him.
How did this elf know Caelira?
"Max!" Nick called from behind.
Max stopped for a moment and looked back.
Nick’s face was filled with worry, and it was clear he wanted to say something more, but he also understood that Max would not turn away from this matter now.
Max looked at him and said solemnly, "After this, I will take care of Munro and Karo forever. Take care out there."
Nick stared at him for a moment, then nodded.
"Be careful," he said.
Max gave a faint nod, then turned around and continued following the golden-haired prince.
Soon, his figure disappeared from Nick’s vision, swallowed by the quieter side of the Combat Hall where fewer participants dared to linger.

The golden-haired elven prince led Max away from the crowded part of the Combat Hall, and the silver-haired elven woman followed quietly at his side, her expression calm on the surface but her eyes still carrying a trace of caution whenever she glanced toward Max.

The three of them moved past several groups of participants, crossed a wide corridor lined with pale stone pillars, and finally entered a secluded area hidden behind a curved wall of smooth white crystal.

This place was much quieter than the main hall. The roars, arguments, and shocked whispers from the Combat Hall became distant and muffled, as if they had been sealed behind layers of invisible barriers, and only a faint silver light flowed across the walls, giving the area a cold and private atmosphere.
Max stopped the moment they reached the center of that secluded space.
He simply stood there and looked at the golden-haired prince with eyes so cold that even the silver-haired elven woman felt her body tense slightly.
Although Starfall Haven’s rules had suppressed his outburst earlier, the rage inside him had not disappeared. It had only been forced under control, like a volcano sealed beneath a layer of ice.
His mother’s name still echoed in his mind, and every time he thought of an elf casually speaking that name, his blood threatened to surge again.
The golden-haired prince turned around and faced him.
For a moment, none of them spoke.
The silence stretched between them like a drawn sword.
Then Max finally opened his mouth.
"How do you know that name?"
His voice was calm now, but that calmness was even more dangerous than his earlier rage.

The golden-haired elven prince looked at Max for a long moment, and although his expression remained calm, there was a heaviness in his eyes that had not been there before, as if even he understood that the words he was about to speak would not be easy for Max to hear.

"I have a guess that you hate the elf race," the golden-haired prince said calmly. "And from what I know, there is indeed a valid reason behind it. I will not deny that what they did was disgustingly wrong, but I need you to trust me here, at least long enough to hear everything."
