Nick’s expression was serious as he continued, "You cannot use strength or release too much energy inside Starfall Haven.
Remember, this is a peaceful city and a neutral zone where killing is prohibited outside the proper battle areas."
Max stared at him for a moment.
Then he slowly took a deep breath.
The rage in his eyes did not disappear, but he forced it down with sheer will.
He understood the situation now.
Starfall Haven had its own rules, and those rules were not something even he could casually ignore.
If he lost control here, the city itself would suppress him before he could act.
"I see," Max said coldly.
He turned back toward the golden-haired prince, released his collar, and stepped back half a pace.
The white light around his body gradually faded once his energy settled, but the killing intent in his eyes remained sharp enough to make the nearby elves tense.
Max looked at the golden-haired prince again and asked, each word controlled but heavy with threat, "How do you know that name?"
The golden-haired prince adjusted his collar calmly, then looked at Max with a gaze that had become far more serious than before.
"Come with me," he said.
After saying that, he turned and began walking toward a secluded area of the Combat Hall, one far away from the demons, humans, and most of the elven participants.
The silver-haired elven woman followed beside him, but she kept glancing back at Max, clearly aware that one wrong word could make this situation explode again.
Max followed without hesitation.
He did not care whether this was a trap.
He did not care whether the golden-haired prince had some hidden motive.
The moment his mother’s name had been spoken, everything else became secondary.
Munro, Karo, the Killing Points, and even the attention of the Combat Hall all faded behind the single question burning inside him.
How did this elf know Caelira?
"Max!" Nick called from behind.
Max stopped for a moment and looked back.
Nick’s face was filled with worry, and it was clear he wanted to say something more, but he also understood that Max would not turn away from this matter now.
Max looked at him and said solemnly, "After this, I will take care of Munro and Karo forever.
Take care out there."
Nick stared at him for a moment, then nodded.
"Be careful," he said.
Max gave a faint nod, then turned around and continued following the golden-haired prince.
Soon, his figure disappeared from Nick’s vision, swallowed by the quieter side of the Combat Hall where fewer participants dared to linger.

The golden-haired elven prince led Max away from the crowded part of the Combat Hall, and the silver-haired elven woman followed quietly at his side, her expression calm on the surface but her eyes still carrying a trace of caution whenever she glanced toward Max.

The three of them moved past several groups of participants, crossed a wide corridor lined with pale stone pillars, and finally entered a secluded area hidden behind a curved wall of smooth white crystal.
This place was much quieter than the main hall.

The roars, arguments, and shocked whispers from the Combat Hall became distant and muffled, as if they had been sealed behind layers of invisible barriers, and only a faint silver light flowed across the walls, giving the area a cold and private atmosphere.
Max stopped the moment they reached the center of that secluded space.
He simply stood there and looked at the golden-haired prince with eyes so cold that even the silver-haired elven woman felt her body tense slightly.
Although Starfall Haven’s rules had suppressed his outburst earlier, the rage inside him had not disappeared.
It had only been forced under control, like a volcano sealed beneath a layer of ice.
His mother’s name still echoed in his mind, and every time he thought of an elf casually speaking that name, his blood threatened to surge again.
The golden-haired prince turned around and faced him.
For a moment, none of them spoke.
The silence stretched between them like a drawn sword.
Then Max finally opened his mouth.
"How do you know that name?"
His voice was calm now, but that calmness was even more dangerous than his earlier rage.

The golden-haired elven prince looked at Max for a long moment, and although his expression remained calm, there was a heaviness in his eyes that had not been there before, as if even he understood that the words he was about to speak would not be easy for Max to hear.
"I have a guess that you hate the elf race," the golden-haired prince said calmly.
"And from what I know, there is indeed a valid reason behind it.
I will not deny that what they did was disgustingly wrong, but I need you to trust me here, at least long enough to hear everything."

chapters.title: Chapter 1731: Max Voidwalker!
paragraphs: Max stared at him with cold eyes.

The secluded area was quiet, and the faint silver light flowing across the crystal walls made his expression look even colder. He did not trust this elf. He did not trust his calm tone, his noble posture, or the way he seemed to know far more than he should.
But the name Caelira had already been spoken, and now that his mother’s past was being placed before him piece by piece, Max could not walk away.
"Go on," Max said calmly.
The golden-haired prince nodded slightly.

"It is like this," he said. "There are currently three factions within the elf race that control almost everything. My faction remains neutral most of the time, and we rarely interfere unless the balance of the race itself is threatened. Then there is the second faction, the most aggressive of the three. Their methods are ruthless, their ambitions are extreme, and they believe the elf race should never bow to the will of any other race or compromise its purity for any reason."
His voice became a little lower.
"That faction should be the one that attacked your home, Max Voidwalker, and took away your parents."
Max’s eyes narrowed instantly.
A chill ran down his spine.
It was not because of fear.
It was because the golden-haired prince had spoken his true name.
Max Voidwalker.

He had made sure not to reveal that name casually, and in Starfall Haven, he had not told this elven prince anything about his real identity. Yet this elf had said it as if he had already known. That single detail made Max’s heart sink slightly, while the killing intent he had just suppressed began stirring again in the depths of his chest.
"How do you know that name?" Max asked, his voice dangerously soft.

The golden-haired prince did not avoid his gaze. "Because once I connected you to Caelira, your identity was no longer difficult to guess. The restricted records did not reveal everything, but they did mention the name of the human man she married and the family name connected to the child she gave birth to."
Max’s fingers clenched slowly.
The prince continued before Max could interrupt further.
"The third faction," he said, "is where your mother was once the leader."
Max’s body trembled slightly.
For a moment, the rage in his eyes was disturbed by shock.
His mother had once been the leader of an elven faction.
No.
Not merely a faction.
He knew that his mother was once an elf and she chose to give up her bloodline and her elf identity for some reason but to think she was a leader of an elf faction was shocking even to Max.
The golden-haired prince’s next words made his mind go still.

"Caelira was once called Divine Queen Caelira," the prince said calmly. "Her faction was the strongest of the three factions, and in a way, she was the true leader of the elf race, recognized by all elves, respected by every major bloodline, and feared even by the most ambitious elders of the second faction."
Max did not speak.
He simply stared at the golden-haired prince.

A part of him wanted to reject those words immediately. His mother, the gentle woman he remembered, the woman who had lived peacefully with his father, the woman who had smiled at him in a quiet home far away from the center of power, had once been the Divine Queen of the elf race.
It sounded absurd. It sounded impossible. Yet the way the prince spoke did not feel like a lie, and that made the revelation even harder to bear.

The golden-haired prince continued, "But something strange happened one day. No one knows the full truth, or perhaps those who know have sealed it away too deeply, but according to the records, Divine Queen Caelira suddenly gave up her royal bloodline and abandoned her identity as an elf. After that, she disappeared."
Max’s breathing became heavier.
The silver-haired elven woman standing nearby lowered her gaze, clearly aware that this was no ordinary secret. Even for her, who served beside the prince, some of these details seemed shocking.

"A few years after she gave up her bloodline and her identity," the golden-haired prince continued, "the elf race received news that she had married a human and was living peacefully on a remote planet far away from the territories ruled by the elves. To many elves, that news was impossible to accept. The queen who was supposed to lead the elven race, the woman whose bloodline represented the highest purity of our royal inheritance, had chosen to live like a mortal beside a human in a distant world."
He paused for a moment before adding, "It was shocking to all elves."
Max’s face remained cold, but his heart was no longer calm.
Images from his childhood flashed through his mind. A quiet home. His mother’s voice. His father’s presence. His sister’s playful side. The warmth of ordinary days that he had once taken for granted.

He had never imagined that behind that peaceful life was a past like this, a past filled with royal bloodlines, factions, forbidden decisions, and an entire race that had once viewed his mother as their queen.
The golden-haired prince’s expression became more solemn.

"At first, even though some of the higher-ups of the second faction were displeased, they did not act. Your mother had already given up her royal bloodline and identity as an elf, and even though her decision was considered disgraceful by many of them, they still chose to respect it on the surface. Perhaps they feared the remnants of her old faction. Perhaps they feared the consequences of touching her. Perhaps they simply believed she no longer mattered."
His eyes sharpened slightly.
"But everything changed when a piece of news leaked."
Max looked at him.
The prince said slowly, "The news said that you, Max Voidwalker, had somehow inherited the Divine Bloodline, a variant born from your mother’s former royal bloodline."
Max’s pupils contracted slightly.

The golden-haired prince continued, "Your mother once possessed the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline, which was already one of the highest bloodlines among the elves. But what awakened in you was different. It was called the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. It was considered a grade above the royal bloodline your mother once held when she was the Elven Queen."
The secluded area became unbearably silent.
Even the silver-haired elven woman looked shaken.

chapters.title: Chapter 1732: Divine Queen Caelira
paragraphs: The golden-haired prince’s voice remained steady, but the weight behind his words grew heavier. "That was when the second faction could no longer remain still. To them, the idea that a half-human child, born far away from the elf race, had inherited a bloodline superior to the queen’s own royal bloodline was something they could not accept. It threatened their pride. It threatened their ideology. More importantly, it threatened their claim over the future of the elf race."
Max’s jaw tightened.
"So they attacked," he said coldly.
The golden-haired prince nodded.
"Yes," he said. "They resorted to an attack, and that attack led to the catastrophe that happened around twenty ago."
The words fell like stones into Max’s heart.
Twenty years ago.
The catastrophe at his home.
His parents being taken away.
His life being torn apart.
All of it had happened because some faction among the elves could not accept his existence.
For a moment, Max said nothing.

His body was still, but the rage inside him was not. It rose slowly, quietly, and more dangerously than before. This was no longer blind anger. This was a cold hatred being sharpened by truth. The second faction had not merely harmed his family by accident.
They had come because of his bloodline. They had come because of his mother’s past. They had come because Max himself had become something they feared, desired, or could not tolerate.
The golden-haired prince seemed to understand what Max was thinking, because he spoke again before Max could sink fully into that rage.
"I am not asking you to forgive the elf race," he said calmly. "I would not forgive them either if I were you."
Max looked at him.

The prince continued, "But you need to understand that the elf race is not united in this matter. The second faction acted, but not all elves supported them, and your mother’s old faction still exists, though it has weakened greatly after her disappearance. There are still many among them who still believe in Divine Queen Caelira and would die fighting for her.

Max’s eyes narrowed as he listened to the golden-haired elven prince speak, and the more he heard, the more complicated the image of his mother became in his mind. He had always remembered Caelira as his mother, as the gentle woman who had lived quietly with his father on a remote planet, the woman whose smile had once made their simple home feel warmer than any palace could ever be.

But now, that same woman was being described as Divine Queen Caelira, the former leader of the elf race, the ruler of the strongest faction, and someone who had once carried the responsibility of guiding an entire race.

To have that kind of position, to possess that kind of bloodline, to stand above countless elves as their queen, and yet still choose to abandon her royal bloodline and give up her identity as an elf just so she could live with her family, was not something Max could accept as a simple romantic decision.
There had to be more to it.
Max could feel it clearly.

His mother’s choice to abandon her race and bloodline could not be as simple as the surface made it seem. A queen did not give up everything without a reason. A woman who once commanded the strongest faction of the elf race would not disappear quietly unless there was something behind that decision, something heavy enough to make her cut away her past, her title, and even the bloodline that had once defined her existence.
Perhaps it was love. Perhaps it was danger. Perhaps it was betrayal. Perhaps it was all of those things together.
The golden-haired prince seemed to understand what Max was thinking, but he did not interrupt his thoughts for long.

"But things are not going well for the faction your mother once belonged to," the prince continued, his voice growing heavier. "After Divine Queen Caelira disappeared, her faction lost its strongest pillar, and although many loyal elders still tried to preserve her influence, the second faction became more aggressive with each passing year."
Max looked at him silently.

The golden-haired prince’s expression darkened slightly. "Recently, they crossed a line. Without holding a proper meeting with our faction, and without receiving any consent from us, the second faction imprisoned nearly every elf belonging to your mother’s old faction. They claimed it was necessary to maintain internal order, but everyone knows that was only an excuse. Their real goal is to weaken her faction completely and make themselves the strongest power within the elf race."
The silver-haired elven woman standing nearby lowered her gaze slightly, and the quiet anger in her eyes showed that even she found the matter shameful.

"Because of this," the golden-haired prince continued, "your mother’s faction has suffered greatly. Their elders are restrained, their resources have been seized, their younger members are watched, and many of their supporters have been forced into silence. Those who once followed Divine Queen Caelira with pride are now treated like criminals in their own home."
Max’s fingers slowly curled into fists.

The golden-haired prince glanced at him, then continued in a calm but bitter tone. "Even though my father, the leader of the first faction, wanted to interfere, he is powerless right now. The second faction has somehow managed to gain the support of several ancestors of our race, and because of that, most of our objections during the internal meetings are ignored or suppressed before they can change anything. In a way, even though it is disheartening to admit, our faction has almost become useless in the current political balance."
Max stared at him.
For the first time, he saw something beyond noble calm in the prince’s face.
Frustration.
Shame.
Helplessness.

This golden-haired elf was not speaking like someone who wanted to manipulate him with lies. He sounded like someone who had watched his own faction lose power little by little, while a more ruthless faction grew bold enough to crush the people who had once followed Max’s mother.
"But there is still a chance," the golden-haired prince said.
Max’s gaze sharpened. "A chance for what?"
"A chance for you to contact the members of your mother’s faction right now."
Max’s expression changed.
"What?" he asked, unable to hide his shock. "I can?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1733: Aunt Caroline
paragraphs: The golden-haired prince nodded. "Did you forget what the Cosmic Ascension Conference is? It allows young geniuses from across the Divine Realm to enter and compete, regardless of race, faction, or territory. Even though the young geniuses from your mother’s faction were imprisoned in the elven home world, the rules of the conference still pulled them into this place when the event began. That means they are somewhere in this world right now."
Max’s eyes shone faintly when he heard that.
For a moment, something stirred inside him that was not rage.
It was hope.

If the young geniuses from his mother’s faction were truly here, then perhaps he could finally meet someone connected to his mother’s past. Perhaps he could learn more about Caelira, about why she abandoned the elf race, about what happened twenty-two years ago, and perhaps even about where his parents were now.

But almost immediately, that hope became mixed with uncertainty. He did not know anyone from his mother’s faction. He did not know whether they would recognize him, trust him, or even accept him. To them, he might be nothing more than the half-human son of the queen who had abandoned them.
The golden-haired prince saw through Max’s concerns almost immediately.

"I do not know whether you are aware of this or not," he said, "but after your mother gave up her royal bloodline and abandoned her identity as an elf, the person who suffered the most was her younger sister, Caroline."
Max froze.
"Mother has a sister?"
The shock in his voice was impossible to hide.

He knew so little about his mother’s family that the revelation struck him harder than he expected. An aunt. His mother had a younger sister. Someone connected to Caelira by blood. Someone who might have known her before she became his mother, before she became the quiet woman living on a remote planet, before she left behind the identity of Divine Queen Caelira.
The golden-haired prince nodded.

"Yes," he said. "Caroline. She was your mother’s younger sister, and after Caelira disappeared, Caroline became one of the people who suffered the worst because of her connection to her. Many elves in the second faction hated her simply because she carried the same royal bloodline and because some members of your mother’s old faction still saw her as the closest remaining symbol of Divine Queen Caelira’s legacy."
Max’s expression turned colder.

The prince continued, "Even now, Caroline and several young geniuses from her faction are being hunted by members of the second faction inside a region of this world called the Eternal Hourglass. If nothing is done, they will be eliminated from the conference. And once they are sent back to our home planet, they will once again be subjected to imprisonment, humiliation, and torture."
The word torture made Max’s gaze turn icy.
For a brief moment, the secluded area seemed to become colder.
The silver-haired elven woman instinctively tensed, because she could feel the killing intent rising from Max again, though this time he controlled it far better than before.
Max took a slow breath.
He thought of his mother.
He thought of the faction that had once followed her.

He thought of a woman named Caroline, his aunt, someone he had never met, someone who had suffered because of Caelira’s choice, and someone who was now being hunted down by the same faction that had destroyed his family.
Then Max made his decision.
"Where is she?" he asked.
The golden-haired prince looked at him.
Max’s voice was calm, but it carried an edge sharp enough to cut through bone.
"Where is Caroline?"

The golden-haired prince did not delay any longer, because he could already see from Max’s expression that the moment Caroline’s safety was mentioned, there was no chance of stopping him from going there.

"She is in a very deadly place," the golden-haired prince said solemnly. "A few hours ago, I received news that in order to flee from the elves of the second faction, Caroline and some members of your mother’s faction escaped into one of the most dangerous zones of the Eternal Hourglass, Witch God Valley."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
The name alone carried a strange heaviness.
"Witch God Valley?" he repeated.

The golden-haired prince nodded. "It is not an ordinary danger zone. The Eternal Hourglass itself is already filled with countless trials and death zones but Witch God Valley is dangerous even by the standards of that place. It is said that an ancient witch god once died there, and although no one knows whether that legend is true or not, the valley is filled with cursed mist, soul-devouring winds, and strange illusions that can make even powerful geniuses lose their direction. Max’s expression remained unchanged.

"Because she had no better choice," the golden-haired prince replied. "The second faction’s hunters were closing in on her from multiple directions, and if she had stayed in the open region of the Eternal Hourglass, she would have been surrounded and eliminated. The golden-haired prince’s expression became heavier.
"Two people are leading the hunt," he said. "The first is Seraphine Lareth."
Max had already heard that name once, and now that it was spoken again, his eyes became sharper.

He did not know whether they would recognize him, trust him, or even accept him.

The golden-haired prince saw through Max’s concerns almost immediately.

chapters.title: Chapter 1734: Elrian Vaelthorn!
paragraphs: The golden-haired prince’s gaze sharpened. "Fin Arclight."
The name made the silver-haired elven woman’s expression change slightly, and Max immediately noticed it.
"He is dangerous?" Max asked.

"Very," the golden-haired prince said without hesitation. "If Seraphine is ruthless and commanding, then Fin is silent and unpredictable. He also possesses the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline, but like Seraphine, his bloodline is not on the same level as your mother’s. It is a downgraded version of the royal bloodline, but his talent in combat is terrifying, and many elves believe that his actual battle instincts are even sharper than Seraphine’s."
Max looked at him with narrowed eyes.
The golden-haired prince continued, "Both Seraphine and Fin possessed Pseudo Cosmic Path and so you have to be extra careful around them.
Max’s gaze turned thoughtful for a moment.
Seraphine Lareth.
Fin Arclight.

Both possessed the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline, both were from the second faction, both had mastered Pseudo Cosmic Paths, and both were hunting his mother’s younger sister inside Witch God Valley.

The golden-haired prince looked at Max carefully and said, "I know you are strong. After watching you crush Karo, I will not insult you by pretending otherwise. But Seraphine and Fin are not ordinary participants, and they are not like the demons you destroyed in the arena. They are among the strongest geniuses of the elf race, and if they work together, even someone at Karo’s level would be in serious danger."
Max’s lips curved slightly.
"Are you warning me not to go?"
"No," the golden-haired prince replied. "I am warning you not to treat them carelessly."
Max’s smile faded, but the cold confidence in his eyes remained.

The prince continued, "You may possess a bloodline even higher than theirs, but you have not lived among elves. You may not fully understand the methods of the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline yet. Seraphine and Fin have trained with that power since childhood, and their Pseudo Cosmic Paths are built around it. They know how to use radiant bloodline pressure, light-based suppression, illusion, restraint, and execution techniques. If you underestimate them only because their bloodlines are downgraded versions of your mother’s, you may suffer for it."
Max looked at him silently for a few breaths.
Then he asked, "Are they stronger than Karo?"
The golden-haired prince did not answer immediately.
That silence was enough to show that the question was not simple.
"Yes. Both of them can one shot Karo if they want to." The elf prince nodded solemnly.
Max slowly nodded.
"I understand."
The golden-haired prince studied him. "Do you?"
Max’s eyes became icy.
"I understand that two people connected to the faction that destroyed my home are hunting my aunt."
The silver-haired elven woman felt a chill run down her spine when she heard his tone.

Max continued, "I understand that both of them have the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline. I understand that both of them have mastered Pseudo Cosmic Paths. I understand that they are among the strongest geniuses of the elf race."
He paused for a moment, then smiled faintly.
"And I understand that if they hurt Caroline before I arrive, I will make them regret entering this conference."
The golden-haired prince stared at him for a long moment.
Then he let out a quiet breath.

"Then go to Witch God Valley as quickly as you can," he said. "If my information is accurate, Caroline and the others are being driven deeper into the cursed region. Once they reach the inner valley, even I do not know what kind of danger they will face."
He added point at the silver haired woman elf. "Also take Nancy here with you. She knows the way to the Witch God Valley and will help you locating Caroline."
Max turned to the silver haired woman elf before looking at the elf prince.
"What is your name?"
The golden-haired prince paused, as if he had not expected Max to ask that now.
"Elrian," he said. "Elrian Vaelthorn."
Max looked at him for a moment, then nodded faintly.
"Elrian," he repeated. "If what you told me is true, then I owe you for this information."
Elrian’s expression remained calm. "Save Caroline first. We can speak of debts later."
Max did not say anything else.
He turned and walked away, his steps calm but filled with a silent killing intent that made even the crystal walls of the secluded area feel colder.
The silver-haired elven woman watched Max walk away from the secluded area, and after a brief silence, she turned toward the golden-haired prince with a calm but serious expression.
"Your Highness, I will see you later."
Elrian looked at her for a moment, then nodded.
"Be careful out there Nancy," he said quietly.
Nancy lowered her head slightly. "I understand."
After saying that, she turned and followed Max without hesitation.
Elrian remained where he was, watching the two of them leave, and his emerald eyes became deeper as their figures disappeared into the distance.
He had given Max the truth, or at least the part of the truth he knew, but even he could not predict what would happen once Max reached Witch God Valley.

If Caroline truly met him, if the young geniuses of Caelira’s old faction learned that Divine Queen Caelira’s son was alive, and if the second faction discovered that Max Voidwalker had reawakened the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline despite being the bloodline source taken away from him, then the balance among the elves might be shattered completely.
Meanwhile, Max and Nancy walked out of the Combat Hall together.

The moment they stepped outside, the loud atmosphere behind them faded, and the open streets of Starfall Haven appeared before them once again. The city was still peaceful on the surface, with pale stone roads, floating lanterns, and silent towers glowing beneath a gentle silver sky, but Max could feel the hidden currents moving beneath that calmness.

News of what had happened inside Arena Seven would not remain contained for long. Karo had died once, his six million Killing Points had been taken, and Max’s name had now entered the attention of humans, demons, and elves alike.
Max did not care about that.
His mind was already focused on Witch God Valley, Caroline, Seraphine, Fin, and the second faction that had destroyed his family.
After walking a short distance from the Combat Hall, Max glanced at Nancy and asked, "What is the fastest way to Witch God Valley?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1735: Leaving Starfall Haven!
paragraphs: Nancy looked toward the distant western side of Starfall Haven, where the city gates stood beneath a curtain of pale light.
"We have to pass through another neutral zone first," she said. "After that, we will reach the outer path leading toward Witch God Valley."
Max nodded slightly.
"I see."
His gaze shifted toward the exit of Starfall Haven.
For a moment, his expression remained calm, but the coldness in his eyes deepened. He had not forgotten Munro. He had not forgotten Karo either.
Karo had died once inside the arena, but he was not truly gone, and Max knew very well that a demon like him would not quietly accept such humiliation.

As for Munro, Max had already decided to settle that matter before leaving the city. If both of them were waiting near the exit, then it would actually save him the trouble of searching for them later.
"Anyway," Max said, his voice calm, "let us go and take care of Karo and Munro first."
Nancy’s eyes moved slightly.
"You think they will be waiting for you?"
Max smiled faintly as he continued walking toward the western exit.
"If I am not wrong, they should already be waiting near the exit of Starfall Haven."
Nancy looked at him in silence for a moment.

She could not tell whether Max was being reckless or simply confident, but after seeing him destroy Karo’s Abyssal Grave of the Fallen with a single fist, she knew his confidence was not baseless. Still, she could not help reminding him, "Starfall Haven is a neutral zone. They cannot attack you inside the city, but the moment you step outside, the rules will no longer protect anyone."
Max’s smile became colder.
"That is exactly why they will wait there."
Nancy’s expression turned solemn.
The streets around them were quiet, but a few participants still recognized Max as he passed. Some humans stopped and stared with wide eyes. Several demons quickly lowered their gazes or moved aside.

A few elves looked at Nancy with surprise, as if they could not understand why she was walking beside the same human who had killed her not long ago. Max ignored all of them and continued toward the exit, his steps steady, his expression relaxed, and his killing intent hidden so deeply that only someone standing close to him could sense how dangerous he truly was at that moment.
Nancy walked beside him and said, "Munro may not be alone. If Karo has already revived and left the Combat Hall, he might have gathered other demons."
"Good," Max replied.
Nancy turned to him.
Max’s eyes remained fixed on the distant gate.
"If they gather more people," he said softly, "then I will not have to hunt them one by one."
Nancy fell silent.

For a brief moment, she remembered the scene of Karo’s Pseudo Cosmic Path shattering under Max’s fist, and she suddenly felt that the ones waiting outside the city might not understand what kind of monster they were preparing to ambush.
The western exit of Starfall Haven grew closer.

Beyond the gate, the peaceful silver light of the city gave way to a darker horizon, where the distant sands of the Eternal Hourglass shimmered like a golden sea under a strange sky. The path leading out was wide and empty, yet Max could already feel several hidden auras lingering beyond the boundary of the neutral zone.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"So they really are there."
Nancy’s eyes sharpened as she also sensed the presences waiting outside.
"How many?"
Max did not answer immediately.

He walked forward until he stood only a short distance from the city’s exit, where the invisible protection of Starfall Haven ended and the outside world began. Then he raised his gaze toward the shadows beyond the gate, his voice calm but filled with cold certainty.
"Enough to make this quick."
With those words, Max stepped toward the exit, and the peaceful rules of Starfall Haven remained behind him.
In no time, Max stepped outside the city gates.

The moment he crossed the boundary of Starfall Haven, the strange peaceful pressure that had restrained all killing intent and violent energy inside the neutral city faded from around his body like an invisible chain being removed.
The air beyond the gate was completely different from the calm atmosphere inside the city. It was heavier, colder, and filled with the faint scent of blood, sand, and demonic energy.

Behind him, the silver-white radiance of Starfall Haven still glowed softly, while ahead of him stretched the darker road leading toward the Eternal Hourglass, where golden sands shifted beneath the distant sky like a restless ocean.
Max did not stop immediately.
He continued walking forward for some distance, as if he had not sensed anything unusual at all.

Nancy followed beside him, but her expression had already turned solemn. She could feel it now. The hidden auras surrounding the area were not few. They were everywhere, concealed behind rocks, shadows, broken ruins, and folds of demonic mist.
The moment they moved far enough from the protection of Starfall Haven, those auras began to stir like predators waiting for prey to step into the center of their trap.
Then, all at once, the world around them changed.
Boom!
Dark demonic energy erupted from every direction.

Thousands of demons appeared out of nowhere, rising from the ground, stepping out from behind distorted shadows, descending from the air, and emerging from clouds of black mist as if an entire army had been lying in wait outside the city gates.

Their bodies were different in size and shape. Some were enormous, with horns curling toward the sky and weapons resting on their shoulders. Some were lean and sharp-eyed, their claws dripping with poison. Some wore black armor covered in demonic runes, while others carried blades, spears, axes, chains, and strange bone weapons that released thick killing intent.
In only a few breaths, Max and Nancy were completely surrounded.
The road behind them was sealed.
The path ahead was blocked.
The empty land on both sides became filled with demons.

Their numbers were so great that the area outside Starfall Haven looked as if it had been swallowed by a demonic tide, and the combined pressure of thousands of hostile auras caused the ground itself to tremble faintly.
Some participants still inside the city gate noticed the sudden movement and quickly stopped to watch from a safe distance, their faces changing when they saw the size of the ambush waiting outside.

The path ahead was blocked.
The empty land on both sides became filled with demons.

Their numbers were so great that the area outside Starfall Haven looked as if it had been swallowed by a demonic tide, and the combined pressure of thousands of hostile auras caused the ground itself to tremble faintly.
Some participants still inside the city gate noticed the sudden movement and quickly stopped to watch from a safe distance, their faces changing when they saw the size of the ambush waiting outside.

chapters.title: Chapter 1736: Surrounded!
paragraphs: Nancy’s eyes narrowed.
"So many..." she muttered.
Max, however, only smiled faintly.

His gaze passed calmly over the thousands of demons surrounding him, and there was not the slightest trace of panic in his expression. Instead, he looked almost amused, as if the scene before him had confirmed exactly what he had expected from the beginning.
At the front of the demon army, two figures slowly walked forward.
The first was Karo.

He looked completely different from the confident demon who had entered Arena Seven with a smile, because although he had revived after death, the humiliation of being killed by Max had not disappeared.
Beside Karo stood another demon.

This demon was taller and broader, with dark red skin, sharp black horns, and a face that bore a faint resemblance to Karo’s, though his features were rougher, colder, and far more brutal. His crimson eyes carried none of Karo’s earlier playful arrogance.

Instead, there was only a deep and savage killing intent, the kind that belonged to someone who did not enjoy long conversations before slaughter. A huge black blade rested against his shoulder, and every step he took caused the ground beneath him to crack slightly.
Max looked at him once and immediately understood.
This was Munro.
The demon he had come to kill.
Karo stopped a short distance away and stared at Max with a twisted smile. "You really came out."
Max looked at him calmly. "Of course I did."
Karo’s eyes twitched slightly when he heard that casual reply.
Munro’s gaze moved from Max to Nancy, then back to Max, and his expression became colder. "So this is the human who killed you once?"
Karo’s face darkened.

The thousands of demons around them heard Munro’s words, and although none of them dared to laugh openly, the air still seemed to shift strangely. Karo felt it clearly, and the humiliation in his heart burned even hotter.
"He used the arena rules and caught me off guard," Karo said coldly.
Max raised an eyebrow.

Nancy glanced at Karo with a strange expression, because she had personally seen Max crush Karo’s Pseudo Cosmic Path in front of everyone, and hearing Karo speak as if his defeat had been caused by carelessness almost made her wonder whether demons truly believed their own lies.
Max smiled faintly. "Caught you off guard?"
Karo’s killing intent surged.

Max continued calmly, "I destroyed your Abyssal Grave of the Fallen, crushed your attack, killed you with one punch, and took your six million Killing Points. If that is called catching you off guard, then I suppose I can do it again."
The demons around them instantly became restless.
Munro’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Karo’s face turned almost savage.

"You will not get that chance again," Karo said through gritted teeth. "This is not the arena. There is no barrier. There is no trial rule. There is no one-on-one battle. Outside Starfall Haven, numbers are also strength."
As soon as he spoke, the thousands of demons around Max and Nancy released their aura at the same time.
Boom!
The combined pressure was terrifying.

Demonic energy rose into the sky like a black storm, covering the area outside the city gates and causing the distant golden sands to shake violently. The sheer number of demons made the scene overwhelming. Even a strong genius would feel suffocated if surrounded by so many enemies, especially with Karo and Munro standing at the front.
Nancy slowly placed one hand on the hilt of her sword.
Her expression was calm, but her eyes were serious.
"Max," she said quietly, "there are too many of them."
Max did not look at her.
He only stared at Karo and Munro.
"There are a lot," Max admitted.
Karo sneered.
Munro gripped the huge blade on his shoulder.
Then Max smiled.
"But not enough."
The moment those words fell, the air around him changed.

A faint draconic pressure began to stir beneath his skin, and although he had not yet transformed, the ground beneath his feet started cracking silently. The demons closest to him instinctively took half a step back, their bodies reacting before their minds could process why. Even Munro’s eyes sharpened, while Karo’s expression twisted with both hatred and caution.
Max slowly rolled his neck and looked around at the thousands of demons.
"You gathered all these demons here for me," he said softly. "Good."
His smile became colder.
"That saves me a lot of time."
Karo stared at him, his eyes burning with fury. "You still dare to act arrogant?"
Max’s gaze returned to him.
"I told you inside the Combat Hall," he said calmly. "If I saw you again, I would kill you again."
Then he looked at Munro.
"And since Munro is here too, I can finish both of you before heading to Witch God Valley."
Munro’s expression turned murderous.
The thousands of demons tightened their formation.
Behind them, Starfall Haven remained silent and untouchable, its peaceful light glowing beyond the city gates, while outside its protection, killing intent flooded the land like a rising tide.
Max stood at the center of the encirclement with Nancy beside him, surrounded by thousands of demons, facing Karo and Munro at the front.
Yet his expression remained calm.
No.
It was not merely calm.
It was expectant.
As if the real hunt had finally begun.

"Do you really think you can stop me with these?" Max asked Karo and Munro, his calm gaze sweeping over the thousands of demons surrounding him before returning to the two figures standing at the front.
"You are arrogant," Munro said in a deep voice. "But arrogance becomes stupidity when it has no place to stand."
Max glanced at him and raised an eyebrow. "And you are Munro?"
Munro’s eyes narrowed. "You know my name."
"I came out to kill you," Max replied calmly. "It would be strange if I did not know the name of the person I am about to erase."
The surrounding demons immediately erupted with furious growls.
"Arrogant human!"
"Kill him!"
"Tear him apart!"
"Let him understand what happens when he offends our demon race!"

Nancy stood beside Max with one hand on the hilt of her sword, her silver hair fluttering slightly in the heavy demonic wind. Her expression remained composed, but her eyes moved across the countless demons surrounding them, measuring their numbers and positions.
Even though she had seen Max’s strength, the scale of this encirclement was still terrifying. Thousands of demons had gathered here, and many of them were not weak.

chapters.title: Chapter 1737: Dimensional Shift!
paragraphs: Karo noticed Nancy’s cautious gaze and sneered. "Even your elf companion understands the situation better than you do. You may have defeated me once, but do not mistake that for invincibility. Outside Starfall Haven, you can be surrounded, exhausted, and buried beneath endless attacks."
Max looked at him for a moment, then laughed softly.
"Karo," he said, his voice carrying a trace of mockery, "after losing six million Killing Points to me, you still dare to speak as if you understand my limits?"
Karo’s expression twisted with fury.
Max continued, "You hid after reviving, gathered a crowd, waited outside the city gate, and now you are talking about strength. If I were you, I would have hidden better."
A few demons instinctively looked toward Karo, and although none of them dared to show it openly, the words clearly struck where it hurt most.
Karo’s aura erupted violently.
"You will regret provoking me again."
Max’s smile disappeared, and his eyes turned cold. "No, Karo. You are the one who should regret showing yourself again."
Munro raised one hand, stopping Karo before he could lose control completely.
His gaze remained on Max, and after a moment, a cruel smile slowly appeared on his face.
"Enough words," Munro said. "Since he thinks thousands of demons are not enough, let him test it with his body."
He lifted his black blade and pointed it toward Max.
The killing intent of the surrounding demons surged at once, rising like a dark tide from every direction.
"Attack," Munro ordered coldly. "Do not let him leave even a bone behind."
The moment his command fell, thousands of demons roared at the same time.
Boom!
The earth shook as the encirclement collapsed inward.

Demons charged from every direction, their weapons raised, their claws extended, their demonic energy erupting like black flames across the battlefield. Some rushed across the ground with savage speed, some leapt into the air and descended like falling meteors, while others began releasing long-range attacks from the back, filling the sky with spears of darkness, poisonous mist, black fireballs, bone arrows, and blood-colored chains.
In an instant, the land outside Starfall Haven turned into a battlefield.
Nancy drew her sword.
Max, however, only stood there and watched the demon tide surge toward him.
Then a faint smile returned to his face.
"Good," Max said softly. "Come together."
His voice was calm, almost pleased, and as the tide of thousands of demons rushed toward him from every direction, he stood in the center of their encirclement with no trace of fear on his face.

Black flames, poisonous mist, bone arrows, blood chains, demonic spears, and savage killing intent filled the space around him, while Nancy tightened her grip around the hilt of her sword, fully prepared to fight her way through the storm if necessary.
But Max did not move to attack.
Instead, he smiled.
"Now let’s try something new," he muttered.
The moment those words left his mouth, a golden light began to bloom from within his body.

It was not the dark chaotic radiance of his Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline, nor was it the starry brilliance of Star Fist. This light was purer, brighter, and more sacred, carrying a noble pressure that seemed to come from something ancient, divine, and immeasurably high.
Golden patterns slowly appeared across Max’s skin, flowing beneath the surface like streams of sunlight, and the air around him trembled as his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline awakened.
Nancy’s eyes widened slightly as she sensed a pressure acting upon her body and it wasn’t just any pressure, it was bloodline pressure.
The demons charging toward Max also felt something strange, but by the time they sensed that the golden light around him was not an ordinary defensive technique, it was already too late.
"Dimensional Shift," Max muttered slowly.
In the next instant, the world changed.
There was no explosion.
There was no violent tearing of space.
There was only a sudden flash of golden radiance that swallowed everything at once.

Before any demon could react, before Karo or Munro could give another order, and before Nancy could even understand what Max had done, the entire battlefield outside Starfall Haven vanished from their senses.
The city gate, the dark road, the golden sands of the Eternal Hourglass in the distance, and the familiar sky above them all disappeared as if they had been wiped away by an invisible hand.
When the demons regained their senses, they were no longer outside Starfall Haven.
They were standing inside a dimension of light.
For a moment, no one moved.

Thousands of demons who had been roaring with killing intent just a breath ago now stood frozen in place, their weapons still raised, their attacks half-formed, their expressions stiff with disbelief. Some of them looked around in confusion, while others took instinctive steps back, unable to understand how the battlefield beneath their feet had changed so suddenly.
"What is this place?"
"Where are we?"
"The city gate... where did the city gate go?"
"Impossible! He moved all of us?"
"No, this cannot be real. This must be an illusion!"
The demons began shouting one after another, but their voices sounded strangely small in the endless world of light around them.
Everywhere they looked, there was radiance.

The sky above was a vast sea of golden-white brilliance, without sun, moon, or stars, yet glowing with an endless light that seemed to come from every direction at once. In the distance stood hundreds of thousands of mountains and hills made entirely from condensed luminance, their peaks shining like divine crystals and their slopes flowing with soft golden mist.

Rivers ran between those light-filled mountains, but even the water did not look like water. It flowed like liquid radiance, clear, bright, and sacred, cascading down from the high cliffs like streams of melted sunlight.
The ground beneath their feet was also formed from light.
It was firm, yet strange.

Every step sent faint ripples of golden brilliance spreading outward, and every ripple carried a soft but oppressive pressure that made many demons feel deeply uncomfortable. Their demonic energy, which usually surged freely and violently, now felt heavy and sluggish in this place, as if the dimension itself rejected their existence.

chapters.title: Chapter 1738: Divine Light of Justice and Truth!
paragraphs: Karo’s expression changed drastically.

He looked around with sharp eyes, and the hatred on his face was quickly replaced by shock and caution. He could still sense the demons around him. He could still sense Munro. He could still sense Nancy. But the outside world was gone, and the thousands of demons he had gathered had been dragged into this strange luminous dimension in a single instant.
"How did he do this?" Karo muttered, his voice low and filled with disbelief.
Munro’s eyes narrowed deeply.

Unlike the ordinary demons, he did not panic immediately, but the grip around his black blade tightened. His instincts were screaming at him that this place was not simple. It was not an illusion, and it was not a normal domain. It felt more real than a domain, wider than a battlefield technique, and far more oppressive than any ordinary spatial skill.

Nancy stood a short distance away from Max, her silver hair glowing faintly beneath the golden radiance surrounding them. She looked at the endless mountains of light, the rivers of luminance, and the sky that seemed to stretch beyond the limits of sight, and for the first time since leaving the Combat Hall, her calm expression broke completely.
"This is..." she whispered.
Max stood at the center of everyone, golden light flowing around his body like divine fire.

His Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline continued to shine, and beneath that light, his presence felt completely different from before. He no longer looked like a human covered in arrogance and killing intent. He looked like the master of this luminous world, a being standing inside a dimension that recognized his authority.
This was the ability of the Dimensional Sovereign Body.
Dimensional Shift.
It allowed Max to shift a portion of any dimension he had unlocked and bring it into the real world, temporarily replacing the battlefield around him with that chosen dimensional space.

It was not as simple as teleportation, nor was it merely dragging people into an illusion. He had brought a real part of a dimension into contact with reality, and everyone caught within the range had been swallowed into it before they could resist.
The demons had not entered this world willingly.
Max had pulled them in.
Thousands of demons, Karo, Munro, and even Nancy had all been shifted into this dimension of light in a single breath.
A demon with three horns suddenly roared, unable to endure the oppressive purity around him any longer, and slammed his axe into the ground with all his strength.
Boom!

The axe landed heavily, but instead of shattering the luminous ground, it only caused a ripple of golden light to spread outward. The demon’s arms shook violently from the rebound, and he staggered back with shock written across his face.
"This place is suppressing us!" another demon shouted.
"My demonic energy is slower here!"
"Damn it, break out!"

Several demons immediately released attacks toward the sky, sending black flames, dark spears, and demonic beams upward, but the moment those attacks rose into the golden radiance above, they were gradually weakened, dissolved, and swallowed by the endless light. The sight made the surrounding demons even more uneasy.
Karo looked at Max with an ugly expression.
"You had this kind of ability?"
Max smiled faintly.
"I told you," he said calmly, "you should have hidden better."
Karo’s face twisted.
Munro stepped forward, his heavy aura erupting around him as he stared directly at Max. "So this is your trump card?"
Max glanced at him, then looked around at the thousands of demons trapped inside the dimension of light.
"No," Max replied with a relaxed smile. "This is only the battlefield I chose."
Those words made the demons’ hearts tremble.
Only the battlefield.
That meant Max had not even begun using the true power of whatever inheritance he had activated.
Nancy looked at him from the side, and for the first time, she understood why Elrian had said Seraphine and Fin were already in danger.

If Max could drag thousands of demons into a dimension of light with a single ability, then what would happen when he faced the elves of the second faction who carried a downgraded version of the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline?
The thought made her heart shake.
Max slowly raised his hand.
The rivers of light in the distance trembled.
The luminous mountains released a faint hum.
The endless golden sky brightened.
The demons surrounding him felt their bodies stiffen as a terrifying pressure descended upon them from all directions, and the same thought appeared in many of their minds at once.
They had not surrounded Max.
Max had gathered them into his own battlefield.
And now, there was nowhere left to run.
"Divine Light of Justice and Truth."
Max’s voice was quiet when he muttered those words, but the moment they left his mouth, the entire Dimension of Light seemed to awaken in response.

The golden sky above the demons trembled, the rivers of light flowing between the luminous mountains began to surge violently, and the endless hills and peaks formed from condensed radiance released a low divine hum that spread across the whole dimension. Then, one after another, enormous golden constructs began appearing in the air.

They were shaped like crosses made entirely from light, and each one looked sacred, sharp, and terrifyingly pure, as if judgment itself had taken physical form. In only a few breaths, there were no longer dozens or hundreds of them.
There were hundreds of thousands of golden cross-shaped light constructs suspended across the entire sky, filling every direction above the demon army with blinding radiance.
Every single light construct released the fifth level concept of space.
That was what made them terrifying.

They did not merely shine with holy light, nor were they simple weapons of radiant energy. Each cross-shaped construct distorted the space around it, causing the air to fold, ripple, and crack under the pressure of Max’s comprehension.

The fifth level space concept wrapped around the golden light like an invisible blade, making every construct appear both near and far at the same time, as if distance itself had become meaningless under Max’s control.

Because they had been summoned inside the Dimension of Light, their power was amplified to an absurd degree, and the entire world around the demons seemed to have become a divine execution ground prepared solely for them.

Dimensional Shift.
It allowed Max to shift a portion of any dimension he had unlocked and bring it into the real world, temporarily replacing the battlefield around him with that chosen dimensional space.
It was not as simple as teleportation, nor was it merely dragging people into an illusion.
He had brought a real part of a dimension into contact with reality, and everyone caught within the range had been swallowed into it before they could resist.
The demons had not entered this world willingly.
Max had pulled them in.
Thousands of demons, Karo, Munro, and even Nancy had all been shifted into this dimension of light in a single breath.
A demon with three horns suddenly roared, unable to endure the oppressive purity around him any longer, and slammed his axe into the ground with all his strength.
Boom!
The axe landed heavily, but instead of shattering the luminous ground, it only caused a ripple of golden light to spread outward.
The demon’s arms shook violently from the rebound, and he staggered back with shock written across his face.
"This place is suppressing us!" another demon shouted.
"My demonic energy is slower here!"
"Damn it, break out!"

Several demons immediately released attacks toward the sky, sending black flames, dark spears, and demonic beams upward, but the moment those attacks rose into the golden radiance above, they were gradually weakened, dissolved, and swallowed by the endless light.
The sight made the surrounding demons even more uneasy.
Karo looked at Max with an ugly expression.
"You had this kind of ability?"
Max smiled faintly.
"I told you," he said calmly, "you should have hidden better."
Karo’s face twisted.
Munro stepped forward, his heavy aura erupting around him as he stared directly at Max.
"So this is your trump card?"
Max glanced at him, then looked around at the thousands of demons trapped inside the dimension of light.
"No," Max replied with a relaxed smile.
"This is only the battlefield I chose."
Those words made the demons’ hearts tremble.
Only the battlefield.
That meant Max had not even begun using the true power of whatever inheritance he had activated.
Nancy looked at him from the side, and for the first time, she understood why Elrian had said Seraphine and Fin were already in danger.

If Max could drag thousands of demons into a dimension of light with a single ability, then what would happen when he faced the elves of the second faction who carried a downgraded version of the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline?
The thought made her heart shake.
Max slowly raised his hand.
The rivers of light in the distance trembled.
The luminous mountains released a faint hum.
The endless golden sky brightened.
The demons surrounding him felt their bodies stiffen as a terrifying pressure descended upon them from all directions, and the same thought appeared in many of their minds at once.
They had not surrounded Max.
Max had gathered them into his own battlefield.
And now, there was nowhere left to run.
"Divine Light of Justice and Truth."
Max’s voice was quiet when he muttered those words, but the moment they left his mouth, the entire Dimension of Light seemed to awaken in response.

The golden sky above the demons trembled, the rivers of light flowing between the luminous mountains began to surge violently, and the endless hills and peaks formed from condensed radiance released a low divine hum that spread across the whole dimension.
Then, one after another, enormous golden constructs began appearing in the air.
They were shaped like crosses made entirely from light, and each one looked sacred, sharp, and terrifyingly pure, as if judgment itself had taken physical form.
In only a few breaths, there were no longer dozens or hundreds of them.
There were hundreds of thousands of golden cross-shaped light constructs suspended across the entire sky, filling every direction above the demon army with blinding radiance.
Every single light construct released the fifth level concept of space.
That was what made them terrifying.
They did not merely shine with holy light, nor were they simple weapons of radiant energy.
Each cross-shaped construct distorted the space around it, causing the air to fold, ripple, and crack under the pressure of Max’s comprehension.

The fifth level space concept wrapped around the golden light like an invisible blade, making every construct appear both near and far at the same time, as if distance itself had become meaningless under Max’s control.

Because they had been summoned inside the Dimension of Light, their power was amplified to an absurd degree, and the entire world around the demons seemed to have become a divine execution ground prepared solely for them.

chapters.title: Chapter 1739: Slaughter!
paragraphs: The thousands of demons looked up.
Their faces changed instantly.

Even the most savage among them felt fear grip their hearts when they saw the endless golden crosses spread across the sky like stars of judgment. The purity of the light suppressed their demonic energy, the space concept sealed their escape routes, and the sheer number of constructs made resistance feel almost meaningless.

Some demons roared and released black flames toward the sky, some formed defensive shields around their bodies, some tried to tear open space and escape the dimension, while others charged toward Max in desperate fury, hoping to kill him before the attack descended.
But Max only lowered his hand.
"Fall."
The sky collapsed in golden light.
Countless cross-shaped constructs descended at once.

They did not fall like ordinary weapons. They vanished from the sky and appeared directly above their targets through distorted space, bypassing distance and ignoring most defensive formations. A demon had just raised his shield when a golden cross appeared over his head and pierced straight through him, splitting his body apart in a burst of divine radiance.

Another demon tried to dodge to the side, but space folded around him, and the cross that should have missed appeared directly in his path, pinning him to the luminous ground before exploding into a storm of light.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Explosions erupted everywhere.
The Dimension of Light became a world of endless judgment.

Golden crosses fell in infinite numbers, striking the demon army from above, from the sides, from behind, and even from beneath their feet as space twisted under Max’s control. Every impact released a burst of radiant force that tore through demonic bodies, shattered armor, burned away dark energy, and crushed the soul-like aura hidden within many of them.
The demons screamed, roared, and cursed, but their voices were drowned beneath the continuous thunder of divine light striking the ground.
Nancy stood beside Max, stunned into silence.
The golden light did not harm her.

It curved around her like flowing water, as if the dimension itself recognized that she was not an enemy. But everywhere else, the demons were being slaughtered. Some tried to gather together and form a huge demonic barrier, but dozens of light crosses descended upon the same point at once, their fifth level space concept overlapping until the barrier was sliced apart from the inside.
Some stronger demons attempted to counterattack, but their skills were swallowed by the endless radiance before they could even reach Max.
This was not a battle.
It was an execution.

Karo’s expression twisted with disbelief and rage as golden crosses descended toward him from every direction. He released his Abyssal Grave of the Fallen again in desperation, causing black-red mist and tombstones to rise around him as he tried to resist the incoming judgment, but compared to the power he had displayed inside the arena, his aura was clearly weaker after losing once to Max.
Even so, the Abyssal Grave still spread outward with terrifying force, forming a grave-like domain around him in an attempt to bury the falling light.
But inside the Dimension of Light, Max’s inheritance technique was far too powerful.
The first wave of golden crosses tore into the black-red mist and split it apart.
The second wave shattered the tombstones before they could fully form.

The third wave pierced directly into the heart of the Abyssal Grave of the Fallen, causing Karo’s Pseudo Cosmic Path to tremble violently. Each cross carried not only divine light, but also the fifth level concept of space, and every impact distorted the structure of Karo’s path until the grave-like domain began collapsing in pieces.
"No!" Karo roared, his voice filled with fury and fear. "Not again!"
Max looked at him from afar with cold eyes.
Then several hundred cross-shaped constructs appeared above Karo at the same time.
They fell together.
Boom!

Karo’s Abyssal Grave of the Fallen shattered completely once more, and before he could escape, the golden crosses pierced through his body from every direction. His demonic energy was torn apart, his body was pinned in the air by radiant spatial force, and in the next breath, he was swallowed by a blinding explosion of golden light.
Karo was killed again.
Munro was not spared either.

When the golden crosses began falling, Munro had already erupted with all his strength. His huge black blade released a terrifying demonic pressure, and his body swelled as dense black-red markings spread across his skin, making him look like an ancient demon war god standing within a storm of light.

He swung his blade again and again, shattering dozens of golden constructs with pure force, and for a brief moment, his strength truly surpassed most of the demons around him. Each slash tore open a dark path through the radiance, and every roar from him sent shockwaves across the luminous ground.
But the constructs did not end.
For every cross Munro shattered, ten more appeared.
For every gap he carved open, space folded and filled it again.

The fifth level space concept made the light constructs impossible to avoid through ordinary movement, and the Dimension of Light strengthened them endlessly, as if the entire world was feeding power into Max’s attack.

Munro’s arms began to tremble. Cracks appeared across his black blade. The demonic markings on his body dimmed beneath the pressure of the divine radiance. Still, he roared and charged forward, his eyes locked on Max with savage hatred.
"Max!" Munro thundered. "Fight me directly if you dare!"
Max looked at him calmly.
"You are not worth that much effort."
Munro’s eyes widened with fury.
The next instant, thousands of golden crosses appeared above him.

Munro raised his blade with both hands and released one final roar, but the endless constructs descended before he could move again. The first hundred shattered his blade. The next hundred pierced through his shoulders, arms, legs, chest, and back.
Then the remaining crosses fell like a golden rain of execution, tearing through his body again and again until his enormous figure was completely drowned in radiant spatial power.
Boom!
Munro exploded into nothingness.
His aura vanished.
His roar disappeared.
Only a wave of Killing Points scattered from the place where he had stood.

chapters.title: Chapter 1740 - 22 Million Points - Rank 7!
paragraphs: Across the battlefield, the slaughter continued.

Thousands of demons were erased one after another beneath the Divine Light of Justice and Truth. Some died screaming, some died trying to flee, some died while begging for mercy, and some died while still attacking in blind rage, but no matter what they did, the result did not change.

The endless cross-shaped constructs fell upon them with merciless precision, and the Dimension of Light became brighter with every demon destroyed, as if their deaths only made Max’s battlefield shine more brilliantly.
Nancy watched the scene with a pale face.
She had known Max was strong.
She had seen him kill Karo once.
But this was different.

This was the power of an inheritance technique combined with his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, his Dimensional Sovereign Body, the Dimension of Light, and his fifth level space concept. It was not merely personal combat strength. It was battlefield domination. Against a single opponent, Max was terrifying. Against an army, he was even more horrifying.
Within a short time, the thousands of demons who had surrounded them were gone.
The demonic tide disappeared.
The roars vanished.
The black flames faded.
Only fragments of dark energy and countless streams of Killing Points remained scattered across the luminous battlefield.

Max stood in the center of it all, golden light flowing around his body while the last cross-shaped constructs slowly faded from the sky. His expression was calm, but the coldness in his eyes had not disappeared. He looked toward the places where Karo and Munro had been killed, then raised his hand.
All the Killing Points left behind by the demons surged toward him like a crimson storm.
At first, they emerged like scattered crimson sparks across the luminous battlefield.
Then those sparks multiplied.

A moment later, they became countless streams of blood-red radiance, bursting from every place where a demon had died and filling the Dimension of Light with a storm of Killing Points so dense that it looked as if an entire crimson galaxy had been shattered and released into the air.

The golden world around them was dyed with red light, and the contrast between the sacred radiance of the dimension and the blood-colored Killing Points made the scene feel both beautiful and terrifying.
Nancy stood silently beside Max, her silver hair glowing beneath the mixture of golden and crimson light.
She could not help looking around in shock.
Thousands of demons had died here.
Karo had died again.
Munro had been killed as well.
All of them had become Max’s reward.
The trial-like system of the Cosmic Ascension Conference began calculating the points from every fallen demon, and in the next instant, the crimson lights surged toward Max from every direction.

They flowed into him like endless rivers, wrapping around his body before disappearing into his form, while the number beside his name began rising at a speed that would have made every participant in the Combat Hall lose their mind.
[Participant: Max]
[Previous Killing Points: 7,000,000]
[Absorbed Killing Points: 15,000,000]
[Current Killing Points: 22,000,000]
[Rank: 7]
The moment the final number stabilized, even Nancy’s breathing paused.
Twenty-two million Killing Points.

This was no longer the kind of amount ordinary participants could even imagine. Max had walked out of the Combat Hall with seven million Killing Points after crushing Karo in the tenth battle, and now, after wiping out the demon army waiting outside Starfall Haven, he had gained another fifteen million in one sweep.
The thousands of demons who had gathered to trap him, including Karo and Munro, had not become his executioners.
They had become his harvest.
Max looked at the number floating before him and smiled faintly.
"Twenty-two million."
His voice was calm, but there was a faint trace of satisfaction in it.
Nancy turned toward him, still struggling to process what she had just witnessed. "You gained fifteen million Killing Points from this one attack."
Max glanced at the fading crimson light around him. "They gathered themselves together for me."
Nancy was silent for a moment.
There was nothing wrong with what he said.
Karo and Munro had truly gathered thousands of demons in one place, surrounded him outside the city gates, and believed that numbers would be enough to bury him.

But Max had dragged them all into the Dimension of Light and turned their ambush into his own execution ground. From beginning to end, they had never controlled the battlefield. They had only stepped into the place Max had chosen for their deaths.
The golden sky above them slowly calmed.
The luminous mountains stopped humming.
The rivers of light returned to their peaceful flow.

Max raised his hand slightly, and the last remaining strands of crimson Killing Points entered his body. Then the notification before him faded, leaving only the quiet brilliance of the Dimension of Light around them.
Nancy looked toward the place where Munro had been destroyed, then toward where Karo had died for the second time, and a complicated expression appeared in her eyes.
"Munro and I think Karo too should have a life left." She said frowning.

"Let it be," Max said calmly as the last traces of golden light around him faded and the Dimension of Light began to withdraw from reality. "I do not think they would dare to hoard points like that again or pull the same conspiracy as last time. As for eliminating them completely, I do not think they would leave Starfall Haven after seeing my true strength, and right now, I cannot be bothered with them anyway."
He then turned to Nancy.
"Let us head toward Witch God Valley."
Nancy nodded, and without wasting another moment, her figure turned into a beam of silver-white light as she shot toward a certain direction across the golden sands of the Eternal Hourglass.

Max followed closely behind her, his speed no slower than hers, and in only a few breaths, the area outside Starfall Haven became silent once again, leaving behind no demons, no ambush, and no trace of the army that had tried to surround him.

chapters.title: Chapter 1741: Proud Moment for the Black Dragon Clan!
paragraphs: At the same time, far away in the territory of the Black Dragon Clan, a completely different scene was taking place.

Above the central region of the clan floated an enormous ranking list that seemed to cover the sky itself. It was formed from ancient black-gold light, and countless names were written upon it in shining characters that shifted and updated in real time.

Every disciple, elder, guardian, and important figure of the Black Dragon Clan could see it simply by raising their head, and because the Cosmic Ascension Conference was one of the most important events of the Divine Realm, this ranking list had become the center of everyone’s attention since the moment the conference began.
This was the Cosmic Ascension Ranking List.
It reflected the current standing of all young geniuses participating in the conference.

At first, the atmosphere in the Black Dragon Clan had been rather heavy, because although several of their disciples had entered the Cosmic Ascension Conference, none of them had managed to enter the top one hundred.

This was not because the Black Dragon Clan was weak, but because the Cosmic Ascension Conference gathered monstrous geniuses from every great race, ancient clan, divine forces, royal bloodline, and hidden inheritance across the Divine Realm.
To enter the top one hundred among such a crowd was already an extremely terrifying achievement, and not every great force could casually produce someone capable of doing it.
Because of this, many elders had been silently watching the list with complicated expressions.
Some were disappointed.
Some were patient.
Some were waiting for one of their clan geniuses to rise later in the conference.
But no one expected what happened next.
The ranking list suddenly trembled.

The massive black-gold characters floating in the sky shifted violently, and the names near the top began to rearrange themselves. At first, the elders thought another supreme genius from some ancient force had gained a large number of Killing Points, but when a new name suddenly shot upward through the rankings at an absurd speed, every gaze in the Black Dragon Clan froze.
The name did not stop at the top one hundred.
It did not stop at the top fifty.
It did not stop at the top twenty.
Instead, under the stunned eyes of everyone present, one name directly rushed into the top ten and stopped at the seventh position.
[Rank 7: Max]
[Killing Points: 22,000,000]
For a moment, the entire Black Dragon Clan fell into absolute silence.
Then the silence exploded.
"What?!"
"Rank seven!"
"Max entered rank seven!"
"Twenty-two million Killing Points! How did he gain that many points all at once?"
"Was he not outside the top one hundred just moments ago?"
"This is impossible. He jumped directly to the seventh rank!"

Countless disciples stared at the ranking list in disbelief, their voices filling the clan grounds like a rising storm. Some of them rubbed their eyes as if they thought they had seen wrongly, while others pointed toward the sky with trembling hands, unable to contain their excitement.
A disciple of their Black Dragon Clan had not merely entered the top one hundred. He had directly charged into the seventh rank of the entire Cosmic Ascension Conference.
That meant Max was now standing above countless geniuses from terrifying forces throughout the Divine Realm.
The elders of the Black Dragon Clan were even more shaken.

For the older generation, they understood the meaning of this ranking far more clearly than the younger disciples. The top ten of the Cosmic Ascension Conference was not a place ordinary geniuses could touch.

Every person ranked there was either backed by an ancient race, born with a heaven-defying bloodline, carrying a supreme inheritance, or possessing battle power strong enough to shake their generation.
For Max to enter rank seven so suddenly meant that he had either obtained an astonishing opportunity or killed a large number of powerful opponents in a very short period of time.
Either way, it was enough to make the Black Dragon Clan’s name resound.
"Hahaha!"
An elder with a long black beard suddenly laughed loudly, his voice shaking the hall beneath him. "Good! Very good! This boy truly did not disappoint us!"

Another elder’s eyes shone with excitement. "To think that not long ago, none of our disciples were even in the top one hundred, yet now Max has directly reached rank seven. This is not just an improvement. This is a declaration to the entire Divine Realm that our Black Dragon Clan has produced a true monster."

"Twenty-two million Killing Points," another elder muttered, still struggling to calm his heart. "Even if he killed ordinary participants continuously, he would not have gained so many points so quickly. He must have killed someone carrying a massive number of points."
"Or an entire group," someone else said.
The words made several elders fall silent for a moment.
Then their smiles became even wider.
If Max had truly wiped out a large force inside the conference, then his strength might be far more terrifying than even they had expected.

Among them, Lady Virelia stood with her gaze raised toward the enormous ranking list, and the moment she saw Max’s name shining at the seventh position, a rare smile appeared on her beautiful face. It was not the polite smile she usually showed before other elders, nor was it the calm expression she wore as a powerful master. It was a genuine smile filled with pride, satisfaction, and a trace of emotion that she did not bother hiding.
She had found Max in the mortal realm.
She had seen his potential when many others would have overlooked him.
She had brought him into the Black Dragon Clan and watched as his strength grew at a terrifying pace.
Now, that same disciple had entered the Cosmic Ascension Conference and reached rank seven in front of the entire Divine Realm.
How could she not feel proud?
